=== 00010000 [PLATE]
Watcom CRT startup trap stub: the whole BEGTEXT segment of cstrt386.obj (CLIB3S), INT3 then JMP back to itself (cc eb fd) followed by 13 NOPs, all 16 bytes contributed by the library module, not by the linker
Pool hint from block triage: crt

Pool: crt  [CLIB3S.LIB(cstrt386) - BEGTEXT head, byte-exact match of the segment's 16-byte LEDATA record; no Function ID hit (only 3 bytes) and no public symbol covers offset 0]
Head of the Watcom C startup module's BEGTEXT segment: INT3 followed by a JMP to itself, so a call or jump landing on the first byte of the loaded image breaks into the debugger and then spins instead of running into the code that follows.
Evidence: Bytes at 00010000 are cc eb fd 90 x13 (read from the binary). The Watcom 10.0a CLIB3S.LIB module cstrt386.obj contains one LEDATA record for its BEGTEXT segment (segment index 3, offset 0, length 0x14) whose 16 data bytes are exactly cc eb fd followed by thirteen 90 padding bytes - the same bytes in the same order, so this is literal content of a CRT object rather than an idiom-based inference. The identical record appears in the 10.0/10.0b copies of cstrt386.obj too, and cstrt386 is a CLIB3S module in all three (workspace/pool_triage/fid/manifest.json). cstrt386's PUBDEF for BEGTEXT names ___begtext at offset 3, i.e. immediately after these three bytes, which is why the trap itself carries no symbol and why no name is proposed. The neighbour verdict at 00010010 (fdps_map_actor_behavior_step, pool fdps, high confidence) confirms the picture: BEGTEXT is 16 bytes of CRT startup object, then _TEXT with game code begins at 00010010. The function has zero callers and zero callees; the only reference to the address is its own backward jump (the DATA xrefs from FUN_00034c10, FUN_0004412f, FUN_00054564 and FUN_00047884 are the immediate constant 0x10000 = 65536 mis-read as an address). Not fdps: no game data, strings or game-side callers. Not ail: no interrupt path, no .DIG driver structure, no touch of 0x70000. Not binary_artifact: it is not synthesised by the linker but shipped inside a library object, and rebuilding will produce it by linking CLIB3S rather than by hand.

=== 00010010 [PLATE]
Advance a single map actor one behavior step.

Algorithm:
Resolves the actor record for the given index through the record accessor at 0002d210 (the same record is reachable as DAT_00069cd8 + index * 0x50, confirming a 0x50-byte stride). If bit 0 of record[5] is set the actor is inactive and the function returns immediately.

Otherwise it reads the behavior mode from the low nibble of record[0x34] and two byte parameters record[0x35] / record[0x36] (a destination pair), plus an event slot index in record[0x3d], and dispatches:
  mode 0, 1, 2, 9  -- try the movement handlers 00012c10 / 000126b0 / 000127c0 / 00012230 in a fixed order and fall back to 000120d0 when every attempt fails. Mode 9 first queries 0002dc20 for a target and, when one exists, walks toward it via 000119e0.
  mode 3           -- like mode 9, but keyed on 00012c10 succeeding first; on a resolved target it clears DAT_00069cd0.
  mode 4, 7        -- clear DAT_00069cd0 and walk toward the record[0x35]/record[0x36] destination via 000119e0. Mode 7, on arrival, plays the "Posion.saf" effect through 00026e00 when the terrain byte record[7] lies in 0x24..0x27, then sets bit 0 of record[5] to retire the actor.
  mode 5           -- event step: if the per-slot flag (&DAT_000640d8)[record[0x3d]] is still clear and 00013e10 yields a destination, walk there; on arrival read a 3-byte entry at DAT_0006013c + slot * 3 + 0x53, copy it into record[0x31]/record[0x32], call 00025d20 when the first byte is zero, set the slot flag, call 0002e910, switch the actor to mode 7 and play "Chess.wav" via 0002a1f0.
  mode 8           -- no action.
  mode 10, 11      -- the interactive/driven modes: 00013040 or 00013420, gated extra handlers 00027180 / 00013c90 when DAT_00063f8c / DAT_00063f88 reach 6, then 00012230, and finally 00012e50 or the 000126b0 / 000120d0 fallback depending on DAT_00063f78. Mode 11 additionally invokes 00010760 when the terrain byte record[7] is in 0x3c..0x3e.

After dispatch it re-reads the record, calls 0002e030 with the actor's current x/y and 1, sets bit 0x80 of record[5] to mark the actor for redraw, and calls fdps_render_view_frame.

Parameters:
  actor_index -- index into the actor record array at DAT_00069cd8 (0x50 bytes per record).
  context     -- second stack argument, passed unchanged to every movement handler.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps

=== 00011460 [PLATE]
Traces the battle movement cost map and returns either a direction path or the nearest reachable unit.

Algorithm:
The global at DAT_00060144 points to a movement map header: word width, word height, then width*height cells of 2 bytes each. Byte 1 of a cell holds the flood-filled step cost, 0xff meaning unreachable. Cell stride is 2 and row stride is width*2; both are computed into locals up front.

mode == 2: scans the unit table (count in DAT_00060150, records fetched by index through FUN_0002d210). Units are filtered by side: when arg4 is zero only units with record byte 6 == 0 are considered, otherwise only units with byte 6 != 0. Units with bit 0 of record byte 5 set are skipped. For each surviving unit the cost cell at (unit.x, unit.y) is read and the minimum is tracked. If no unit was found the function returns -1, otherwise it stores the winning unit's x and y into out_path[0] and out_path[1] and returns the minimum cost.

mode == 0 or 1: starts at (arg4, arg5) and repeatedly steps to the neighbouring cell with the lowest cost, recording one direction code per step into a local buffer: 0 = y-1, 1 = x+1, 2 = y+1, 3 = x-1, 4 = no move. Edge neighbours are skipped at the map borders. If the starting cell is already 0xff the function returns -1 immediately. Mode 0 takes a neighbour only on a strictly lower cost, which makes runs of identical cost keep the current heading. Mode 1 also accepts an equal cost, but only when the previously recorded step used a different direction code, which makes ties alternate direction instead of running straight. The walk stops once the current tile equals (arg1, arg2). The recorded direction codes are then copied into out_path in reverse order and the step count is returned.

Parameters:
arg1 goal_x   - x of the tile at which the walk terminates (unused in mode 2)
arg2 goal_y   - y of the tile at which the walk terminates (unused in mode 2)
arg3 out_path - byte buffer receiving the reversed direction codes, or the found unit's x,y in mode 2
arg4 start_x  - x of the tile the walk starts from; in mode 2 this is the side filter instead
arg5 start_y  - y of the tile the walk starts from (unused in mode 2)
arg6 mode     - 0 straight-preferring trace, 1 turn-preferring trace, 2 nearest-unit query

Returns:
Number of direction codes written in modes 0 and 1, the minimum cost found in mode 2, or -1 when the start tile is unreachable or no unit matched.

Pool: fdps
Battle-map path tracing: walks a per-tile movement-cost grid from a start tile, choosing at each step the cheapest of the four neighbours (with a mode that forbids reversing the previous step), and either returns the nearest reachable enemy unit or writes the reversed direction sequence into the caller's path buffer.
Evidence: Pure game logic with no library character: it reads the game's map-header globals at 0x00060144 (grid pointer, width/height words, stride computed as 2 and 2*width) and the unit-count global at 0x00060150, loops over unit records via fdps_get_unit_record, tests unit flag bits at record offsets +0x05 and +0x06, and emits direction codes 0-3 (with 4 as 'none') into a 0xb0-byte stack path buffer that it then reverses into the caller's output. Callers are all named game code (fdps_battle_move_unit_toward, fdps_battle_unit_turn, FUN_000126b0) and the sole callee is fdps_get_unit_record. No fid hits at all, no CRT idioms (no float/emulator stubs, no DGROUP or heap access, no string primitives), and nothing touching the DOS interrupt path, .DIG driver structures or the 0x70000 AIL state area, so crt and ail are both excluded; at 1161 bytes with a full stack frame and nested loops it is far too large and too map-specific to be a thunk or compiler helper. Existing tags backbone/pool_fdps/subsys_battle agree with the disassembly.

=== 000119e0 [PLATE]
Battle movement: walk a unit toward a requested destination tile.

Algorithm:
1. Resolve the unit record for unit_index via FUN_0002d210, and cache from it: field 0x00 = tile x, field 0x01 = tile y, field 0x20 = movement points, field 0x3b = a movement/terrain cost selector.
2. FUN_00018b70(move_points + 1) yields a per-unit movement context; malloc(100) is the step buffer (one direction code per step) and malloc(0x800) is the reachable-tile list (x,y byte pairs).
3. Build the movement/cost map (FUN_00010b90(map_mode) then FUN_00010de0(ctx, x, y, cost_selector)) and try to path from the unit to (dest_x, dest_y) with FUN_00011460(x, y, step_buf, dest_x, dest_y, 0). It returns the step count, or -1 when no path exists.
4. If that fails, retry the path with the relaxed flag 1. If the relaxed path exists, replay it step by step (direction code 0 = y+1, 1 = x-1, 2 = y-1, else x+1), probing each tile with FUN_0002ba00(x, y) and reading the occupancy result at 0x00069d0c. The last tile whose probe is not 0xff becomes the new destination, i.e. the request is retargeted to the furthest usable tile along the blocked route.
5. Rebuild the movement map, call FUN_000118f0(unit_index, map_mode) to flood the unit's reach, and FUN_00011da0(tile_buf) to collect the reachable tiles and their count.
6. Scan the reachable tiles and keep the one minimising Manhattan distance |tx - dest_x| + |ty - dest_y| to the destination, breaking ties on the smaller ||dx| - |dy|| (the more diagonal-balanced tile).
7. Path to that chosen tile with FUN_00011460(..., 0). If the step count is non-zero, FUN_0002d2d0(unit_index, step_buf, step_count) performs the actual move and the result is 1; otherwise 0.
8. Free both buffers and return.

Parameters:
  dest_x     [ebp+0x14] requested destination tile x; reassigned internally when the route is retargeted
  dest_y     [ebp+0x18] requested destination tile y; likewise reassigned
  unit_index [ebp+0x1c] index of the acting unit, resolved to its record by FUN_0002d210
  map_mode   [ebp+0x20] selector handed to the movement-map builder FUN_00010b90 and to FUN_000118f0

Returns:
  1 if a move of at least one step was executed, 0 if the unit stays where it is.

Pool: fdps
Picks a destination tile for a unit's move: fetches the unit and class records, allocates a path buffer and a candidate-tile buffer, traces reachable tiles, scores each candidate by Manhattan distance and axis balance from the target, then re-traces the path to the best tile and plays the move animation.
Evidence: 945-byte __cdecl frame-pointer function with no Function ID hits at all. The body is entirely game-domain: it calls fdps_get_unit_record(0x2d210), fdps_get_class_record(0x18b70), fdps_map_load_tile_info(0x2ba00), fdps_move_path_trace(0x11460) and fdps_animate_move_path(0x2d2d0), reads unit fields at +0x00/+0x01 (tile x,y), +0x20 (class id), +0x3b, walks a direction byte array with the four cases 0/1/2/else stepping y+ / x- / y- / x+, and checks the map tile result byte at global 0x00069d0c against 0xff. Its only library use is crt_malloc/crt_free (0x3d375/0x3d478) for two scratch buffers and crt abs (0x3d364) inside the distance metric, which is consumption of the runtime, not membership in it. Callers are fdps_map_actor_behavior_step and fdps_battle_system_menu plus three unnamed battle-range functions, so it sits inside the battle subsystem call graph. Not crt (no library match, domain data structures), not ail (no interrupt path, no .DIG driver structure, no 0x70000 state area), not binary_artifact (large real body with local frame and control flow).

=== 00013fd0 [PLATE]
Draws one SAF tilemap layer.

Algorithm:
Takes a 0x24-byte draw context whose field 0x14 holds the base address of a loaded SAF file and whose field 0x18 holds the tilemap index. Reads the section 1 (tilemap) descriptor from the SAF header: item count at 0x16, offset-table start at 0x18. Returns immediately if the index is negative or not less than the item count. Otherwise resolves the tilemap record via saf + *(u32 *)(saf + saf[0x18] + index * 4) and reads its i16 column count and i16 row count, then advances past the 4-byte tilemap header to the cell array. Copies the whole 0x24-byte context onto the stack as a working copy (memcpy at 0x3d514) and iterates rows outer, columns inner. At the start of each row the working copy's x (offset 0x0c) is reset from the caller's x; for each cell the signed i16 tile index is stored into the working copy's index field (offset 0x18), the per-cell tile drawer at 0x13ed0 is called with the working copy, x is advanced by the SAF cell width (header 0x07) and after the row y (offset 0x10) is advanced by the SAF cell height (header 0x09). Cell indices are read signed while the caller's tilemap index is unsigned; the per-cell drawer performs its own range check.

Parameters:
  ctx - pointer to the 0x24-byte SAF draw context: 0x0c = x, 0x10 = y, 0x14 = SAF base pointer, 0x18 = tilemap index on entry (reused as tile index for each cell).

Returns:
  Nothing. Draws nothing when the tilemap index is out of range.

Pool: fdps

=== 00014140 [PLATE]
Draws one composite sprite entry: a bank-indexed group of part records blitted at offsets from a common origin.

Algorithm:
1. Read the bank pointer from req+0x14 and the entry index from req+0x18. The bank header holds an unsigned 16-bit entry count at bank+0x0C and an (unaligned) 32-bit offset-table displacement at bank+0x0E. If the index is negative or >= the count, the lookup yields NULL and the function returns without drawing.
2. Otherwise entry = bank + *(int32 *)(bank + *(int32 *)(bank+0x0E) + index*4), i.e. table entries are bank-relative offsets.
3. Copy the caller's 0x24-byte draw request onto the stack as a scratch request, so per-part edits never touch the caller's copy.
4. Walk the part records, which start at entry+0x0A and are 13 bytes each; the signed 16-bit count is at entry+0x08. Each record holds: u16 sub-sprite id at +0, s16 dx at +2, s16 dy at +4, u8 mode at +6, s16 level at +7 (unaligned).
5. For each part, when req+0x20 in the caller's request is zero the record's mode byte selects the blend setup: mode 0 clears the scratch request's mode field to 0; mode 1 stores 0x10 - level into a small parameter block built from the two runtime tables at 0x000653F0 and 0x000643F0, sets the scratch mode field to 9, and points the scratch request at that block. Any other mode leaves the previous setup in place.
6. Set the scratch request's X to req+0x0C + dx, its Y to req+0x10 + dy, its sprite id to the record's u16, and call the per-part blitter at 0x00013FD0 with the scratch request.
7. After the loop, if the flag argument is non-zero, call 0x000142D0 with the bank pointer and the entry's leading u16.

Parameters:
  req  - pointer to a 0x24-byte draw request: X at +0x0C, Y at +0x10, sprite bank pointer at +0x14, entry index at +0x18, blend parameter block pointer at +0x1C, blend mode at +0x20.
  flag - when non-zero, run the post-draw call at 0x000142D0 for this entry.

Returns:
  Nothing. Silently does nothing when the entry index is out of range.

Pool: fdps
Walks a sprite's part list (13-byte records) from an animation table, computing each part's screen x/y from the draw context and issuing a per-part blit, then optionally triggering a sound effect for the frame.
Evidence: Disassembly is game-specific composite-sprite drawing: it indexes a frame table via [ctx+0x14]/[ctx+0x18] with a bounds check, copies a 0x24-byte draw descriptor with the memcpy-like helper at 0003d514, loops over part count at [+8] stepping the record pointer by 0x0d, adds part dx/dy to context x/y at [ctx+0xc]/[ctx+0x10], calls fdps_draw_tilemap_layer (00013fd0) per part, and finally calls fdps_sfx_play (000142d0). === 00014550 [PLATE]
Advance a SAF animation playback cursor by one tick.

Algorithm:
The cursor is a 3-dword state block: [0] current frame index, [1] tick counter inside the current frame, [2] pointer to the loaded SAF image. When mode == 1 the call is a reset: both counters are zeroed and 0 is returned without touching the SAF. Otherwise the SAF header is sanity-checked by comparing the magic bytes 'S', 'A' and 'F' at offsets 0, 1 and 2 (note the original code accepts the file if ANY one of the three matches, not all three), and the frame count is taken from the u16 at header offset 0x0C; a zero frame count makes the function return -1. The tick counter is then incremented and the current frame record is located as saf + *(i32 *)(saf + *(i32 *)(saf + 0x0E) + index * 4), with the index bounds-checked against the frame count (an out-of-range index yields a null frame pointer). The frame's hold time is the i16 at frame offset 0x02; while the tick counter stays below it the frame is held. Once the counter reaches the hold time it is cleared and the frame index is incremented. If the index then reaches the frame count the animation has completed one pass: the tick counter is cleared and, when mode == 0, the index wraps to 0 to loop, otherwise it is clamped to the last frame so playback stops on the final frame; the function returns 1 in that case.

Parameters:
cursor - pointer to the 3-dword playback state block described above.
mode - 1 resets the cursor, 0 loops back to the first frame at the end, any other value holds on the last frame.

Returns:
1 when the animation just passed its last frame, 0 while it is still playing or after a reset, -1 when the SAF data is unusable (bad magic or zero frame count).

Pool: fdps
Advances one animation tick for a SAF animation playback state: validates the 'SAF' magic on the clip header, reads the frame count at header+0xc and the frame offset table at header+0xe, compares the per-frame duration at frame+0x2 against the elapsed counter, and steps or wraps/holds the current frame index.
Evidence: The disassembly compares the referenced buffer's first three bytes against 0x53/0x41/0x46 ('S','A','F'), the game's own animation container magic, then walks a clip header (frame count at +0xc, frame offset table at +0xe) and a per-frame duration field — a resource-format-specific state machine that exists in no C runtime, maths library or sound driver. No fid hit at all, no floating-point, no DOS interrupt path, no .DIG driver structure or 0x70000 state area access, which rules out crt and ail. It has 0 callees and 12 callers, all of them game-side (including fdps_title_screen and fdps_show_game_over), which is the shape of a shared game helper, not a linker thunk or compiler helper — and at 386 bytes with a full stack frame it is far too large to be a binary_artifact.

Algorithm:

Each pass:
  1. Clears cmd_disabled[0] and the global at 0x00069cec, then probes availability:
     - FUN_00025140(unit, 0) == -1  -> cmd_disabled[0] = 1 (command 0 unusable);

  2. Scans cmd_disabled[0..3] for the first zero entry and uses it as the initial

  3. FUN_00016130 draws the menu, FUN_00016200 runs the selection loop and writes the

=== 00016200 [PLATE]
Modal four-way menu cursor input loop.

Algorithm:
Loops until a terminating key arrives. Each iteration reads one scan code
(masked to a byte) from the low-level keyboard reader at 0x000567be and
dispatches on it:
  0x01 (Esc) or 0x53      -> result = -1 (cancel), loop ends
  0x1c (Enter) or 0x39 (Space) -> result = 1 (confirm), loop ends
  0x48 (Up)    -> if dir_blocked[0] == 0 then *cursor_dir = 0
  0x4b (Left)  -> if dir_blocked[1] == 0 then *cursor_dir = 1
  0x4d (Right) -> if dir_blocked[2] == 0 then *cursor_dir = 2
  0x50 (Down)  -> if dir_blocked[3] == 0 then *cursor_dir = 3
A non-zero entry in dir_blocked suppresses movement in that direction, so the
cursor keeps its previous value. Any other scan code falls through unhandled.
After dispatch every iteration unconditionally calls 0x0002eab0 and 0x00015be0
(frame pacing / presentation), then calls 0x00015860(ctx, dir_blocked, 0x18,
*cursor_dir) to repaint the cursor, then repeats.

Parameters:
  ctx          - opaque context/handle forwarded unchanged as the first
                 argument of the redraw call at 0x00015860.
  dir_blocked  - pointer to four ints indexed by direction (0 up, 1 left,
                 2 right, 3 down); zero means that direction is selectable.
                 Also forwarded to the redraw call.
  cursor_dir   - in/out pointer to the currently selected direction index;
                 updated in place on an accepted arrow key.

Returns:
  1  on confirm (Enter or Space)
  -1 on cancel (Esc or scan code 0x53)
The function never returns while the loop result is still 0.

Pool: fdps
Blocking menu-navigation loop: reads a keyboard scancode, maps ESC/Del to cancel, Space/Enter to confirm, and the arrow keys to a direction index gated by a four-entry neighbour table, then cycles the scene palette and redraws the cursor until a result is chosen.
Evidence: The disassembly is pure game UI logic over PC/XT keyboard scancodes (0x01 ESC, 0x53, 0x39 Space, 0x1c Enter, 0x48/0x50/0x4b/0x4d arrows), writing 0/1/2/3 direction codes through a caller-supplied out-pointer and indexing a struct at +0/+4/+8/+0xc for allowed moves. === 000170c0 [PLATE]
Frame-paced input wait loop for the unit status window.

Algorithm:
Copies a 15-entry sprite Y-position table from 0x14818 (15, 30, 70, 105, 140, 170, 150, 130, 150, 170, 160, 165, 165, 160, 170 -- a drop from the top of the screen followed by two bounces) into a local array, and sets the idle-animation frame counter to -1 (inactive). When the flag argument is non-zero it samples the CRT helper at 0x42cf8 and, when the value is a multiple of 200, arms the idle animation by setting the frame counter to 0.

It then loops: poll the input source at 0x178f0; a returned code greater than 0x7f means nothing selected yet, so a frame is drawn. A frame is skipped entirely unless the global tick at 0x69d64 differs from the last-drawn tick at 0x63fc0.

Per frame: allocate a 0x15180-byte 360x240 backing buffer and a 0xfa00-byte 320x200 work buffer, zero the work buffer, capture the current screen into the backing buffer (from 0xa0504 when the mode flag at 0x60070 is set, otherwise via the helper at 0x2bf60), copy it back into the work buffer, then free the backing buffer. The walk-cycle frame index is (tick at 0x63fc0 % 16) / 4, with 3 folded back to 1, giving the 0,1,2,1 cycle; it selects one of three sprite pointers inside the 0x30-byte per-unit record at the table based at 0x60138, whose four 0x0c-byte groups (offsets 0x00, 0x0c, 0x18, 0x24) are the four facings. A 0x240-byte 24x24 scratch buffer receives the decoded cel via the cel blitter, is blitted into the caller's window image at offset 0xd21 (column 161, row 10), and the window image is then blitted into the work buffer as a 0x123 x 0xc8 region at offset 0xf.

When the idle animation is armed, the frame counter drives four phases -- frames 0..14 draw the facing-0 sprite at the table's Y positions (the drop and bounce), frames 15..24, 25..34 and 35..44 draw the other three facings standing at row 170 -- after which a separate Y counter starting at 170 walks the sprite upward in steps of 4 until it passes row 10, at which point the frame counter returns to -1 and the sprite goes back to the plain walk cycle.

The work buffer is presented to VGA memory at 0xa0000 (whole 64000-byte copy when the mode flag is clear, otherwise a 0x138 x 0xc0 rect blit at 0xa0504), both remaining buffers are freed, and the last-drawn tick is updated.

Parameters:
  window_image -- pointer to the 320-pitch composed status window image; the unit sprite is stamped into it at offset 0xd21 each frame
  unit_index -- index into the 0x30-byte-per-entry sprite pointer table at 0x60138; overridden by the global at 0x63fb0 when the mode flag at 0x60070 is set
  allow_idle_animation -- non-zero enables the randomly triggered drop/bounce/turn/rise idle sequence

Returns:
  The input code returned by the poller at 0x178f0 once it is <= 0x7f.

Pool: fdps
Runs the unit status window's animated presentation loop: allocates two off-screen buffers, blits scene layers and sprite cels into them, copies the result to the VGA framebuffer at 0xa0000, and spins polling for input until a key code above 0x7f is returned.
Evidence: 1125-byte __cdecl function with no Function ID hit at all. The body is pure game presentation logic: it touches the VGA framebuffer literal 0xa0000 / 0xa0504, allocates 0x15180 and 0xfa00 (64000 = 320x200) byte buffers via crt_malloc and releases them via crt_free, and calls the game's own fdps_draw_scene_layers (0002bf60), fdps_blit_rect (0002f2f0), fdps_cel_blit_sprite (0002dba0) and fdps_blit_dispatch (000568db) with 0x18x0x18 tile and 0x140-pitch arguments. It reads game state globals (0x60138 unit table base, 0x63fc0 / 0x69d64 tick counters, 0x60070 video mode flag, 0x643dc cel handle) and steps a frame-driven animation state machine keyed on a counter at [EBP-0x24]. Its callers are game code (fdps_battle_show_unit_status_window and FUN_00025b20). Nothing here resembles a C runtime routine, a maths/emulator helper, or Miles AIL (no interrupt path, no .DIG driver structures, no 0x70000 state area), and it is far too large and stateful to be a linker thunk or compiler helper.

=== 00017990 [PLATE]
Modal two-option (left/right) prompt loop.

Algorithm:
1. Allocates a 0x561E byte buffer and copies a 302x73 (0x12E x 0x49) region of
   VGA memory at 0xA9609 into it at stride 302. The caller has already drawn the
   prompt panel there, so this captures the panel bitmap. The four corner pixels
   (offsets 0, 0x12D, 0x54F0, 0x561D) are then cleared to 0 so the later masked
   blit renders the panel with transparent (rounded) corners.
2. Loops until a confirm or cancel key arrives. Each iteration:
   - calls the per-frame update helper at 0002EAB0 and allocates a 0x15180 byte
     (360x240) off-screen work buffer;
   - if the flag at 00060070 is zero, hands the work buffer to 0002BF60 to draw
     the background; otherwise copies the current 312x192 screen area at 0xA0504
     into the work buffer at offset 0x21D8 (x=24, y=24, stride 360);
   - masked-blits the captured panel into the work buffer at offset 0xC4FD
     (x=29, y=140) via 0002F390;
   - if the pointer at 00060120 is non-null, draws it through 000568DB at work
     buffer offset 0x9AD0 (x=32, y=110);
   - draws the two option graphics from the cel sheet at 000643DC at x=249 and
     x=275, y=123. The unselected side uses a fixed cel (13 for the right slot,
     8 for the left); the selected side cycles a 4-frame animation, cels 4..7 on
     the left and 9..12 on the right, indexed by ((frame/3)%4);
   - waits for vertical retrace by polling port 0x3DA (bit 3), blits the work
     buffer back to the screen at 0xA0504 (312x192), spins until the tick
     counter at 00069D64 changes, records it as the animation frame, and frees
     the work buffer;
   - reads a scancode via 000567BE: 0x1C (Enter) or 0x39 (Space) confirms and
     keeps the current selection; 0x01 (Esc) or 0x53 (Del) exits with -1;
     0x4B (Left) selects 0; 0x4D (Right) selects 1. Codes >= 0x7F are ignored.
3. Frees the captured panel buffer and returns the selection.

Selection starts at 0, so the left option is highlighted on entry.

Parameters: none.

Returns: 0 or 1 for the confirmed option (left or right), -1 if cancelled.

Pool: fdps
Modal two-choice yes/no prompt: allocates a save buffer and a scratch scene buffer, draws the prompt window and the two cursor sprites, polls the keyboard scancode for left/right/Enter/Esc while syncing on the VGA retrace port, then frees its buffers and returns the chosen index.
Evidence: Pure game UI logic: calls fdps_blit_rect, fdps_blit_dispatch, fdps_cel_blit_sprite, fdps_draw_scene_layers, fdps_cycle_scene_palette and reads game globals (0x60070, 0x60120, 0x643dc, 0x69d64); the only runtime calls are crt_malloc/crt_free for its buffers and an inport helper at 0x3d4e4 used to poll VGA status port 0x3da. Advances the battle to the next turn.

Algorithm:
1. Clears the input-enabled flag at 0x00060159, allocates a 0x15180-byte (360x240) offscreen map buffer via 0x0003d375 and renders the battle map into it with 0x0002bf60.

Returns: nothing.

=== 00023050 [PLATE]
Loads one 12-sprite group from an open .CEL sheet into the global sprite cache.

Algorithm:
1. fseek(fp, 0x0F, SEEK_SET) and fread a fixed 0x2970 bytes (2652 u32 = 221 groups x 12) of the CEL offset table into a temporary malloc'd buffer, then free it after use. The offset table position 0x0F is hardcoded; the header field at 0x05 is never read.
2. Copy the 13 offsets [group_index*12 .. group_index*12+12] into a local array. Entry 12 is the start of the next group and acts as the end sentinel, so group_bytes = off[12] - off[0].
3. If the cache is empty (count at 0x69CF0 == 0): record the group key in the key table at 0x64060, malloc 0x5A0 + group_bytes for the cache buffer at 0x60138, seek to off[0], read group_bytes directly after the 0x5A0 header area, and fill the 12 pointer-table slots with byte offsets 0x5A0 + (off[i] - off[0]). The write cursor at 0x6411C becomes 0x5A0 + group_bytes. Returns slot 0.
4. Otherwise scan the key table for group_index; on a hit return that slot immediately without touching the cache or the count.
5. On a miss, append: store the key, realloc the cache to cursor + group_bytes, seek and read the group at the cursor, fill pointer-table slots (count*12 + i) with cursor + (off[i] - off[0]), advance the cursor and increment the count. Returns the new slot index.

The 0x5A0-byte header region holds exactly 30 slots of 12 u32 offsets; nothing bounds-checks the slot count against 30, so a 31st distinct group would write its pointer table over the cached pixel data. The fixed 0x2970-byte table read is larger than the offset table of a 1920-sprite sheet and spills into pixel data, but only the entries of the requested group are used.

Parameters:
  group_index - index of the 12-sprite group within the sheet (sprite index = group_index * 12 + i)
  fp          - FILE * for the already-opened .CEL sheet; the file position is left inside the sheet

Returns:
  int - cache slot index for the group, valid for the pointer table at the head of the cache buffer

Pool: fdps

=== 00023bc0 [PLATE]
Adds a character to the unit roster.

Algorithm:
Computes the destination slot as g_roster_base[g_roster_count] where the entry
stride is 0x50 bytes. Looks up two per-character tables by id: a base record
(FUN_00018ab0) and a growth table (FUN_00018ae0). Level is base_record[2].
Max HP = *(int16*)(base+3) + growth[6] * (level - 1);
max MP = *(int16*)(base+5) + growth[8] * (level - 1).
The entry is then filled: +5 = 0, +6 = 2 (side/team tag), +7 and +8 = the
character id, +9 = 0, +0x0a = 0x40, +0x0b = base[0x0c], +0x0c = 0x40,
+0x0d = base[0x0d]. Four two-byte slots at +0x0e..+0x15 are copied from
base[0x0e..0x11]; each slot's flag byte is 0x80 when the source value is 0xff
(empty) and 0 otherwise. Two further slots at +0x16 and +0x18 are set to 0x80
(empty). Four bytes are copied from base+8 to entry+0x1a, +0x1e = 0,
+0x1f = base[0], +0x20 = base[1], +0x21 = level, six bytes at +0x22 are
cleared, +0x31 = 0xff. Three level-scaled stats follow:
+0x37 = *(int16*)(base+0x12) + growth[0] * level,
+0x39 = *(int16*)(base+0x14) + growth[2] * level,
+0x3e = *(int16*)(base+0x16) + growth[4] * level;
+0x3b = base[7], +0x3c = 0. Current and maximum HP are stored at +0x40/+0x42
and current and maximum MP at +0x44/+0x46. Finally FUN_00023ac0 is called with
the new slot index and the roster count is incremented.

Parameters:
  char_id - character/unit identifier, used as the lookup key for both the base
            record and the growth table, and stored in the entry at +7 and +8.

Returns:
  Nothing. The new entry is written into the global roster array and the global
  roster count is incremented.

Pool: fdps
Builds a new 0x50-byte unit record at index [0x00064114] in the roster array based at [0x00064108], filling it from two per-character table entries (base stats and per-level growth) with level-scaled HP/MP/move values, clearing the equipment and inventory slots, then calling 00023ac0 and incrementing the roster count.
Evidence: Pure game logic: 0x50-byte record layout written field by field (flags 0x80/0x40 sentinels, 0xff empty-slot marker, a 4-iteration equipment loop, level-1-scaled stat growth), driven off two game globals at 0x00064108/0x00064114. === 00023e20 [PLATE]
Loads the saved game FDE.SAV and restores the whole game state from it.

Algorithm:
1. malloc(0x59cb) for the raw save image; on failure print "Out of Memory on get save buffer!!!" and exit(1).
2. fopen("FDE.SAV", "rb"), fread(buf, 1, 0x59cb, fp), fclose.
3. Descramble the image (0x000568b7) and recompute its checksum (0x00056898); if the result differs from the dword stored at buf+0x59c7 the save is corrupt: blank the screen (0x000205b0), blit a warning message (0x0001ff60 with source 0xaa44a at 320,208 size 0x140x0xd0) and run 0x00020820.
4. Fan the image out into the global state:
   - buf+0x08a3, 0xa00 bytes -> buffer pointed to by [0x00064108]

Parameters: none.

Returns: nothing. Does not return at all when a malloc fails, because the error path calls exit(1).

Splits the second argument into a signed byte index (arg2 / 8, compiled as the SAR/SBB divide-by-power-of-two idiom) and a bit index (arg2 % 8, computed with IDIV by 8 and taking the remainder). ORs the mask for the bit index into the byte at base + 0x1a + byte index, i.e. base[0x1a + n/8] |= 1 << (n % 8). Nothing is read back and nothing is returned. Parameters: arg1 at [EBP+0x14] is the handle or record selector passed straight through to the resolver at 0x2d210; arg2 at [EBP+0x18] is the signed bit number within the flag array at offset 0x1a. Returns: nothing; EAX is left holding the resolved record pointer as a side effect only.

C entry point of FDPS. Called by the Watcom startup routine at 0004df4c, which pushes _argc (0006a3b4) and _argv (0006a3b8) and passes this function's return value to exit().

Algorithm:
  1. access("DISK.NO", 0) via INT 21h AH=43h. A non-zero result means the game was
     never installed: print "\nCan't found file 'Disk.No' !!!\a\n" and
     "Please use install function.\n", then exit(1).
  2. fopen("Disk.no", "rt"), three fscanf(fp, "%s", ...) reads and fclose(). The first
     two tokens go to a stack buffer and are discarded; the third is stored in the
     global string buffer at 000643e8. Sets the global at 00069d54 to -1.
  3. Calls the CD-ROM presence check at 0003c636 (returns a 16-bit value, sign-extended
     by CWDE). Anything other than 1 prints
     "Fatal error: CDROM is not install!!!\a\n" and "Check your CDROM please!!!\n",
     then exit(1).
  4. Subsystem init: 000304e0(0x19) and 00029660(), then int386(0x10, &regs, &regs)
     with regs.ax = 0x13 to enter VGA 320x200x256 mode.
  5. Clears the state globals (00069cf0, 00069cdc, 00069da0) and the quit flag at
     000643eb, calls 0002a2b0() once, then loops while the quit flag is zero:
       - 0002bae0() pumps one iteration;
       - the request code left in 00069da0 is dispatched: 0 does nothing, 1 runs
         0002a960() followed by 0002a2b0(), 2 calls the handler taken from the
         function-pointer table at 00060304 indexed by the mode selector in 00069cf4
         and then 00031210();
       - the request code is reset to 0 at the end of every iteration.
  6. Shutdown: 00029440(), 000305a0(), 0003c4a7() (pairs with the CD check),
     int386(0x10, &regs, &regs) with regs.ax = 3 to return to text mode, and finally
     prints "\nThank you for playing Flame Dragon Plus!! \n\n".

Parameters:
  argc, argv - passed on the stack by the startup code but never read by this function.

Returns:
  Nothing meaningful. Control falls off the end of the function, so EAX holds whatever
  the final print call left there; the startup code feeds it to exit(). In C source
  terms this is a main() with no return statement.

Pool: fdps
The game's C main(): parses/validates the command line and environment, verifies the CD-ROM is present, initialises audio, sets video mode 0x13 via an INT 0x10 helper, then runs the outer game loop of title screen, battle player phase, village phase and game over until the quit flag at 0x643eb is set, finally restoring text mode and printing an exit message.
Evidence: Disassembly is a hand-written game driver, not library code: it calls fdps_cdrom_detect (0003c636), fdps_audio_init (000304e0) with parameter 0x19, fdps_title_screen (0002a2b0), fdps_battle_player_phase_loop (0002bae0), fdps_run_village_phase (00031210) and fdps_show_game_over (0002a960), dispatches through a game function-pointer table at 0x60304 indexed by the state word at 0x69cf4, and drives game-state globals (0x69cf0, 0x69cdc, 0x643eb, 0x69da0). Loads one named entry from a VFS archive into newly allocated memory.

Algorithm:
1. Calls the VFS directory loader at 0x00039ab0 with the archive path (first stack argument). The returned pointer is the in-memory directory table whose entries are 0x1a bytes wide (size at +0x1e, file offset at +0x27, as used by 0x00039bd0).
2. If the directory pointer is NULL, prints "file not found: '%s'" (format string at 0x00061df8) with the archive path and terminates via exit(1).
3. That callee locates the entry by name, opens the backing VFS file, allocates a block of the recorded size, seeks to the recorded offset and reads the entry in. Its return value (the allocated block, or NULL) is stored into the local result slot.
4. If the result is NULL, calls 0x000567a0 and terminates via exit(1).
5. Frees / closes the directory table via 0x0003d478 and returns the allocated block.

Parameters:

Returns:

Pool: fdps

=== 0002af60 [PLATE]
Builds the global palette helper tables used by the shading and colour-matching code.

Algorithm:
1. Copies the 18-entry brightness coefficient table at 0002ae40 onto the stack. The coefficients are {0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,16,15,14,13,12,11,10,9,8}, indexed by shade level.
2. For each of the 256 palette entries: reads the three bytes (r,g,b) of the source palette (each a 6-bit VGA component, scaled by 4 to 8 bits), packs them as r<<16|g<<8|b, then calls the three component extractors (0002ae90 red, 0002aec0 green, 0002aef0 blue). Each component is masked with 0xF0 and repositioned so the result holds the high nibble of red in bits 16-19, green in bits 8-11 and blue in bits 0-3. Level row 0 of the ramp table (000653f0) is zeroed (black) and this packed value is stored into level row 1 (000657f0, i.e. 000653f0 + 0x400).
3. For levels 2..17, each of the 256 packed row-1 values is multiplied by the level coefficient and stored at 000653f0[level*256 + index]. Because each channel occupies only the low nibble of its own byte, a multiply by up to 16 scales all three channels at once without carrying between them.
4. Fills the 16x16x16 inverse lookup cube at 000643f0: for every (r,g,b) triple of 4-bit components (passed as component*4) it calls the nearest-colour matcher at 0002b1b0 with the source palette and stores the returned palette index as a byte, written sequentially over 4096 entries.

Parameters:
  palette - pointer to 256 packed 3-byte RGB entries (VGA 6-bit components) in r,g,b order.

Returns:
  Nothing meaningful. EAX holds a leftover loop counter; the decompiler models it as an int return but no caller uses it.

Pool: fdps
Builds the game's palette lookup tables: packs the 256-entry RGB palette passed in as a parameter into 24-bit values at 0x657f0, generates 16 brightness-scaled shade rows into the 0x653f0 table, then fills a 16x16x16 RGB-to-palette-index cube at 0x643f0 by calling fdps_palette_find_nearest_color for every quantised colour.
Evidence: The disassembly is application-specific graphics setup, not library code: it writes three game-owned global tables (0x643f0, 0x653f0, 0x657f0), reads a caller-supplied 3-byte-per-entry palette buffer, and copies an 18-dword constant scale table from 0x2ae40 into a local. Its only caller is fdps_load_global_resources and it calls fdps_palette_find_nearest_color plus three local component-extraction helpers -- no CRT or AIL entry point is touched. The fid list is empty, so there is no Watcom library match; there is no DOS interrupt path, no .DIG driver structure and no access to the 0x70000 AIL state area, ruling out ail; and at 580 bytes with three nested loops it is far too substantial to be a thunk or jump island.

=== 0002b1a4 [EOL]
Alignment padding: two 6-byte Watcom NOP forms (lea eax,[eax+0] / lea edx,[edx+0]).

=== 0002b1b0 [PLATE]
Finds the palette index whose RGB triple is closest to a requested color.

Algorithm: keeps a running best squared distance seeded with 10000000 and a running best index seeded with 0x100. Walks a fixed 256 iterations over the palette, consuming three consecutive bytes per entry (red, green, blue in that order) through an advancing byte cursor. For each entry it forms dr = r - pal[0], dg = g - pal[1], db = b - pal[2] and computes dr*dr + dg*dg + db*db as signed 32-bit arithmetic. If that sum is strictly less than the current best it becomes the new best and the loop counter becomes the new best index. The loop count is hardcoded to 256 and is not derived from any argument, so the palette buffer must hold at least 768 bytes. The strict less-than test makes the first of several equally close entries win. The 0x100 seed can never survive because the maximum possible distance is 3*255*255 = 195075, well below the 10000000 seed, so the function always returns a value in 0..255.

Parameters: r, g, b are the target color components, passed as full 32-bit ints and only compared as such (the palette bytes are zero-extended, the targets are not masked). palette points at the first byte of a 256-entry, 3-bytes-per-entry RGB table.

Returns: the 0..255 index of the closest palette entry.

Pool: fdps
Scans a 256-entry RGB palette table, computes the squared Euclidean distance of each entry against a target r/g/b passed on the stack, and returns the index of the closest colour.
Evidence: Disassembly is a plain 256-iteration loop over a caller-supplied byte pointer reading three components per entry, three IMULs summed into a distance, min tracked in a local, index returned; no library call, no data/string reference, no interrupt or driver-structure access. The fid list is empty, so there is no Watcom CLIB3S/MATH387S/EMU387 match, and no C runtime or Miles AIL routine performs palette nearest-colour matching. Its only caller is fdps_build_palette_tables@0002af60, already game graphics code, and the body is unoptimised EBP-frame stack-variable code typical of the game's own translation units rather than a compiled library object. Too large and too purposeful to be a linker thunk or compiler helper, ruling out binary_artifact.

=== 0002b4f0 [PLATE]
Interactive battle-map cursor / target selection loop.

Algorithm:
Reads the map dimensions from the header at 0x00060144 (tile width at +0, tile height at +2) and converts them to pixel extents by multiplying by the 0x18 tile size. When mode == 6 the candidate list length is stashed and then forced to zero, so list cycling is disabled in that mode. If a candidate list is supplied and the first candidate's unit record byte at +7 is not 'y', the cursor is snapped onto that candidate via fdps_map_cursor_move_to using its tile coordinates from unit record bytes +0 and +1 (unit records are 0x50 bytes, base pointer at 0x00069cd8).
FUN_00056799 yields the pointer to the current keyboard scancode byte; it is reset to 0xFF before the loop and after a cancel. Each iteration calls fdps_cd_music_repeat_poll, then reads the scancode:
  0x01 (Esc) / 0x53 (Del)  -> result = -1, loop ends
  0x39 (Space) / 0x1C (Enter) -> confirm. In mode 6 the whole unit array (count at 0x00060150) is scanned for a unit standing on the cursor tile that fails FUN_000109b0; if none blocks, FUN_00018b70 and FUN_0002ba00 are consulted and the tile cost byte read through 0x00069d09 must be below 0x14 for the confirm to succeed (returns 1). Outside mode 6, mode 5 confirms nothing; otherwise FUN_0002ba00 resolves the tile under the cursor and the resolved index at 0x00069d0c must not be 0xFF; mode 4 then returns 1 directly, other modes call FUN_000109f0 with the cursor tile, the clamped value of 0x00069cd0 and the mode, and set the result to 1 when it accepts.
  0x2C (Z) / 0x4C (numpad 5) -> advance to the next entry of the candidate list (wrapping) and snap the cursor to that unit.
  0x48/0x50/0x4B/0x4D (arrows) -> move the cursor one tile (0x18 pixels) in Y (0x00069ccc) or X (0x00069cd4), clamped to the map extents, each move playing "Beep.wav" through FUN_0002a1f0. A repeat counter suppresses movement while the same scancode has been held for 1..5 iterations, giving the usual key-repeat delay.
After key handling the view origin (0x00069ce0 for Y, 0x00069ce4 for X) is scrolled by whole tiles so the cursor stays inside the visible window, and fdps_render_view_frame redraws.

Parameters:

Returns:

Pool: fdps

=== 0002ba00 [PLATE]
Loads the per-cell map information for one battle map tile into the shared "current tile" globals.

Algorithm:
1. Reads the terrain layer pointer at 0x00069cb0. The layer header stores the map width as a 16-bit value at offset 7 and the cell array (one 16-bit tile id per cell) starts at offset 0xb. The linear cell index is y * width + x; the tile id read from that slot is stored to the global at 0x00069d04.
2. Uses that tile id to index the tile attribute table pointed to by 0x00069c98: entries are 4 bytes each and begin at offset 0x11 of the table. The four bytes of the entry are copied out individually, in the order byte2 -> 0x00069d09, byte0 -> 0x00069d08, byte1 -> 0x00069d0a, byte3 -> 0x00069d0b.

4. Indexes a third layer pointed to by 0x00060148, whose own width field lives at offset 7 of its header and whose cell array is one byte per cell starting at offset 0x10. The byte is zero-extended and stored to the 16-bit global at 0x00069d06.

=== 0002bae0 [PLATE]
Player-phase interactive loop on the battle map.

Algorithm:
Obtains the shared keyboard-state byte via the low-level key accessor at 0x56799 and primes it to 0xFF. Reads the map dimensions from the header pointed to by 0x60144 (word 0 = width, word 1 = height) and converts both to pixel extents by multiplying by the 24-pixel tile size. Then loops until the local exit flag becomes non-zero.

Each iteration polls input (0x30c50), reads the current scancode and maintains an auto-repeat counter: the same scancode as last time increments the counter, a different one resets it and records the new code. An action is only taken when the counter is 0 (first press) or greater than 5 (auto-repeat has kicked in); F1 (0x3B) and F2/Home (0x3C/0x47) are handled on the suppressed path instead.

Scancode dispatch:
  0x48/0x50 (up/down)    move the cursor Y at 0x69CCC by one tile, clamped to the map height
  0x4B/0x4D (left/right) move the cursor X at 0x69CD4 by one tile, clamped to the map width
                         each accepted move calls the feedback routine at 0x2A1F0 with the descriptor at 0x61E78
  0x01/0x2C/0x4C/0x53    cycle forward through the unit table: starting from the saved rotation index,
                         scan up to unit-count (0x60150) entries of the 0x50-byte records based at 0x69CD8
                         and stop at the first with (flags[+5] & 0x85) == 0 and side[+6] == 2, then centre
                         on it via 0x2D7C0 with its tile coordinates scaled by 24, saving the next index
  0x1C/0x39 (Enter/Space) clear the key latch (0x567B3), resolve the unit under the cursor (0x2DAA0);
                         with no unit, open the battle menu (0x14AB0) and take its return as the exit flag;
                         with a unit that is friendly (side[+6] == 2), not marked done (flags[+5] & 0x80)
                         and with byte +0x26 clear, open the unit command menu (0x15470) and, if the
                         phase-end flag 0x69DA0 is still clear, run the post-command step (0x2EA10);
                         otherwise show the read-only unit info screen (0x16AA0)
  0x3B (F1)              invoke the routine at 0x2E160
  0x3C/0x47 (F2/Home)    resolve the unit under the cursor and show its info screen (0x16AA0)

After dispatch the camera origin (X at 0x69CE4, Y at 0x69CE0) is scrolled by one tile whenever the cursor comes within one tile of a viewport edge, clamped so the viewport (0x138 by 0xC0 pixels) stays inside the map. The frame is then drawn by 0x2BEB0, and the loop exits once the phase-end flag at 0x69DA0 is non-zero.

Parameters:
None. The decompiler's param_1/param_2/unaff_EBX are artifacts; no incoming stack slot or register is read before being written.

Returns:
Nothing.

Pool: fdps

Evidence: The disassembly is pure game logic: it dispatches on IBM PC keyboard scancodes (0x48/0x50/0x4b/0x4d arrows, 0x1c Enter, 0x39 Space, 0x3b F1, 0x47 Home, 0x53, 0x4c), walks a unit array at global 0x00069cd8 with a 0x50-byte stride testing flag bits at +5 and a side byte at +6 (==2), scrolls the map viewport globals 0x00069ccc/0x00069cd4/0x00069ce0/0x00069ce4 in units of 0x18, and calls only named fdps_ battle/map/render/audio routines (fdps_play_sfx, fdps_map_cursor_move_to, fdps_battle_unit_turn, fdps_battle_show_unit_status_window, fdps_battle_system_menu, fdps_battle_map_overview, fdps_battle_end_phase_if_all_units_done, fdps_render_view_frame, fdps_cd_music_repeat_poll). === 0002beb0 [PLATE]
Renders and presents one frame of the framed main view.

Algorithm:
1. malloc(0x15180 = 86400) a scratch scene buffer. The buffer is a composite: the first 0x21d8 (8664) bytes are header/state, the pixel plane starts at +0x21d8 and is 360 bytes per scan line.
2. FUN_0002bf60(buf) fills/initialises the buffer (shared helper, 21 callers).
3. FUN_0002dcf0(buf) composes this view's content into it (called from nowhere else).
4. Busy-wait on inp(0x3DA) until bit 3 is set, i.e. until vertical retrace begins.
5. FUN_0002eab0() runs inside the retrace window (4 callers; typical of DAC/palette programming).
6. Busy-wait on inp(0x3DA) until bit 3 clears, i.e. until retrace ends.
7. FUN_0002f2f0(buf + 0x21d8, 0x168, 0xA0504, 0x140, 0x138, 0xC0) blits the composed image to VGA memory: source stride 360, destination 0xA0000 + 0x504 (row 4, column 4 of a 320-wide mode 13h screen), destination stride 320, 312 x 192 pixels. That is exactly the interior of a 4-pixel border around the 320x200 screen.
8. Spin until the interrupt-driven tick counter DAT_00069d64 differs from the last-seen value DAT_00069d10, then latch DAT_00069d10 = DAT_00069d64. This paces the caller to one tick per frame.
9. free(buf) and return.

Parameters: none. Everything drawn is taken from global state, which is why 41 different call sites can invoke it with no arguments.

Returns: nothing.

Pool: fdps
Allocates an 86400-byte (0x15180) offscreen frame buffer, draws the scene layers and the cursor info panel into it, waits on the VGA vertical retrace via port 0x3DA, cycles the scene palette, blits a 320x200-ish rect from buffer offset 0x21d8 to video memory, syncs two page-flip globals, then frees the buffer.
Evidence: Disassembly is pure game presentation logic: it calls fdps_draw_scene_layers (0002bf60), fdps_draw_cursor_info_panel (0002dcf0), fdps_cycle_scene_palette (0002eab0) and fdps_blit_rect (0002f2f0), with crt_malloc/crt_free only as the allocator. === 0002bf60 [PLATE]
Composites the scrolling layer table into a scene buffer.

The layer table is a fixed 6-slot structure-of-arrays block in .data, each array 6 dwords or 6 bytes long and packed back to back: pos_x[6] at 0x69bf0, pos_y[6] at 0x69c08, unknown_a[6] at 0x69c20, vel_y[6] at 0x69c38, vel_x[6] at 0x69c50, scroll_factor_y[6] at 0x69c68, scroll_factor_x[6] at 0x69c80, unknown_b[6] at 0x69c98, image[6] at 0x69cb0, mode[6] (bytes) at 0x69cf8 and depth[6] (bytes) at 0x69cfe. The number of active slots is DAT_00069cdc.

Algorithm:
1. Tick gate: if the interrupt tick counter DAT_00069d64 differs from the last value this function
   latched in DAT_00069d14, add vel_x[i] to pos_x[i] and vel_y[i] to pos_y[i] for every active slot,
   then latch DAT_00069d14 = DAT_00069d64. Position therefore advances once per tick regardless of
   how many times per tick the function is called.
2. FUN_0002c220 fills a local 6-entry array with the slot indices in draw order.
3. Pass one, in that order: for each slot whose depth byte is below 10, compute
   x = (DAT_00069ce4 * scroll_factor_x[i] + pos_x[i]) >> 3 and
   y = (DAT_00069ce0 * scroll_factor_y[i] + pos_y[i]) >> 3 -- a per-slot multiple of the two global
   camera/scroll values plus the slot's own accumulated offset, in 1/8 pixel fixed point -- and call
   FUN_0002c330(buf, image[i], unknown_a[i], DAT_00060144, x, y, unknown_b[i], mode[i]).
4. Draw the mid-layer content into the same buffer: FUN_0002c6a0(buf) then FUN_0002d240(buf, 0).
5. Pass two: the identical loop and blit call for every slot whose depth byte is above 10, so those
   slots land on top of the mid-layer content. Depth exactly 10 is drawn by neither pass.

Parameters:
  buf -- destination scene buffer, passed straight through to every drawing callee.

Returns: nothing.

Pool: fdps
Advances per-layer scroll accumulators when the scene state changes, then walks the game's sprite/layer list twice -- once for entries whose depth key at 0x69cfe is below 10 and once for those above -- computing scaled screen coordinates and calling the 8-argument blit routine FUN_0002c330 for each, with a post-pass through FUN_0002c6a0 and FUN_0002d240.
Evidence: No Function ID hits at all against CLIB3S/MATH387S/EMU387, and nothing in the body resembles a runtime primitive: it is a large (689-byte) __cdecl routine driven entirely by a block of game-specific globals at 0x69bf0-0x69d64 (parallel per-layer arrays of x/y positions, deltas, tile handles, palette/flag bytes) plus a count at 0x69cdc and a shared surface pointer at 0x60144. The arithmetic is fixed-point screen positioning (IMUL by a scroll scale then SAR 3), i.e. rendering logic, not library work. It touches no DOS interrupt path, no .DIG driver structures and no 0x70000 state area, so it is not Miles AIL. It is far too large and stateful to be a thunk or compiler helper. Its 21 callers are game UI/scene routines including the already-named fdps_prompt_two_choice and fdps_unit_status_window_wait_input, and its callees are the neighbouring graphics helpers -- the call graph sits wholly inside game code.

=== 0002d7c0 [PLATE]
Animated move of the map cursor to a target pixel position, with viewport follow.

Algorithm:
Reads the map dimensions from the header pointed to by DAT_00060144 (word[0] = width in tiles, word[1] = height in tiles) and converts them to pixels by multiplying by the 24-pixel tile size. Computes dx = target_x - cursor_x (DAT_00069cd4) and dy = target_y - cursor_y (DAT_00069ccc); returns immediately when both are zero. Picks the axis with the larger absolute delta as the major axis and derives the step count n = abs(major delta) / 24, i.e. one iteration per tile of travel. The major axis advances by (major delta / n) each step; the minor axis uses a running accumulator that adds (acc / n) and carries (acc % n) forward, so the two axes stay proportional without floating point.

After each step the viewport origin is clamped so the cursor stays inside its scroll margins: vertically the cursor must sit between 0x18 and 0x90 pixels below the view top (DAT_00069ce0), horizontally between 0x18 and 0xd8 pixels right of the view left (DAT_00069ce4). When a clamp pushes the view past the map edge it is pulled back to map_pixel_height - 0xc0 or map_pixel_width - 0x138 (the 192x312 visible map window), and negative origins are pinned to 0. A local flag records whether the viewport actually moved; the map is redrawn through FUN_0002beb0 when it moved or when the forced-redraw flag DAT_00069cd0 is non-zero.

Parameters:

Returns:
  void. Side effects are on the globals: cursor position DAT_00069cd4 / DAT_00069ccc and viewport origin DAT_00069ce4 / DAT_00069ce0.

=== 0002e710 [PLATE]
Renders the scaled (zoomable) battle map overview into an offscreen 320x200 buffer.

Algorithm:
Reads the current map dimensions from the map header pointed to by the global at 0x00069cb0: width = *(int16*)(hdr+7), height = *(int16*)(hdr+9). Converts the requested camera centre into a top-left world position by subtracting step*0x9c horizontally and step*0x60 vertically (0x9c=156 and 0x60=96 are half the 312x192 viewport), so the caller passes the point that should land at the centre of the view.

World coordinates are 1.12-style fixed point with 0xc00 units per map tile and 0x80 units per source pixel, i.e. every tile is 24x24 pixels (0xc00/0x80 = 24). The top-left position is split into tile index (world / 0xc00) and sub-tile remainder (world % 0xc00), with a manual floor correction that adds 0xc00 to the remainder and decrements the tile index when the remainder is negative, so negative camera positions still sample the correct tile.

The destination buffer is first cleared to colour 0 over its full 64000 bytes, then drawing starts at buffer + 0x504 (row 4, column 4) and advances by 0x140 (320) bytes per output row.

For each of 192 output rows the sub-tile Y remainder is converted to a source row offset ((rem >> 7) * 0x18) inside the tile bitmap. Rows whose tile Y is outside [0, height) are skipped, leaving the cleared background. Otherwise the tile bitmap pointer is fetched from the caller-supplied pointer table as table[tileY * 64 + tileX] (the table has a fixed stride of 64 entries per map row) and the row offset is added.

For each of 312 output columns one byte is copied from the tile bitmap at source column (subX >> 7), skipped when tile X is outside [0, width). After each column the sub-tile X remainder advances by step; when it reaches 0xc00 the tile X index advances, the remainder wraps by subtracting 0xc00, and the tile bitmap pointer is re-fetched from the table. The same wrap logic advances tile Y between rows. Tile X and its remainder are restored from the saved row-start values before each new row.

The step parameter is therefore the zoom factor in source-pixel fixed point: 0x80 gives 1:1, larger values zoom out, smaller values zoom in.

Parameters:
  dest       - destination 320x200 8bpp offscreen buffer, cleared to 0 first
  world_x    - camera centre X in 1/0x80-of-a-pixel fixed point (0xc00 per tile)
  world_y    - camera centre Y in the same fixed point
  step       - fixed-point source step per output pixel, i.e. the zoom factor
  tile_table - array of pointers to 24x24 tile bitmaps, indexed [tileY * 64 + tileX]

Returns:
  Nothing. EAX at RET holds the leftover loop counter and carries no meaning.

Pool: fdps
Clears a 64000-byte 320x200 framebuffer and blits a battle map into it by walking 0xc0 rows and 0x138 columns with a 12.10-style fixed-point scale step (0xc00 units per tile), fetching each source tile pointer from a caller-supplied 64-column table and copying one pixel per step.
Evidence: Game rendering logic, not library code: it reads a global game state pointer at 0x00069cb0 for the map width/height fields at +7/+9, uses hard-coded FDPS screen geometry (0x140 stride, 0xc0 rows, 0x138 visible columns, 0xfa00 = 64000 byte clear, 0x18-byte tile row stride, 64-entry-wide tile pointer table) and per-tile fixed-point stepping of 0xc00. Its only caller is the already-named fdps_battle_map_overview@0002e160 and its only callee is the memset-shaped FUN_00042cd0(dst, 0, 0xfa00). The fid array is empty, so there is no Watcom CLIB3S/MATH387S/EMU387 match; nothing here touches the DOS interrupt path, the .DIG driver structures or the 0x70000 AIL state area, and at 508 bytes with a full stack frame it is far too substantial to be a thunk or compiler helper.

=== 0002ea10 [PLATE]

=== 0002eab0 [PLATE]
Advances the VGA palette colour-cycling animation for the current scene.

Algorithm:
1. Copies about twenty short byte ramps out of read-only tables at 0002b2a0..0002b4e9 onto the stack. The ramps come in R/G/B triples; every byte is a 6-bit VGA DAC component (observed range 0..63). Each ramp is (count + count/... ) bytes long so that a sliding window of `count` entries can start at any phase without wrapping: e.g. a 5-colour cycle stores 9 bytes, a 15-colour cycle stores 29 bytes.
2. Calls fdps_cd_music_repeat_poll (00030c50) as per-frame housekeeping.
3. Gates on the frame tick: if the last-serviced tick at 00069d20 already equals the current tick at 00069d64 the function returns without touching the palette, so the animation advances at most once per tick.
4. Switches on the scene / screen id at 00069cf4 (cases 0, 2, 8, 0x14, 0x15, 0x16, 0x17, 0x1a, 0x1c, 0x1d). Each case picks its own R/G/B ramp triple, its own DAC start index (0xf0, 0xf5, 0xf6 or 0xf8) and its own colour count (5, 7, 9, 10, 11 or 15).
5. Advances the shared phase counter at 00069d24 as (phase + 1) mod (count * 4) — the times-four factor makes the cycle advance one colour every four ticks — then derives the window offset as phase / 4 and calls FUN_0002f240(first_index, r + offset, g + offset, b + offset, count) with cdecl argument order (the caller does ADD ESP,0x14).
6. Records the serviced tick by storing 00069d64 into 00069d20.

Unrecognised scene ids fall through to the tick bookkeeping and change no colours.

Parameters: none. All inputs are globals: 00069cf4 scene id, 00069d20 last serviced tick, 00069d24 cycle phase, 00069d64 current frame tick.

Returns: nothing.

Pool: fdps
Per-frame palette animation driver: gated on a tick counter, it switches on the current scene/screen id and advances a phase index modulo a per-scene period, then feeds three per-scene RGB ramp tables (copied from rodata into stack buffers) to the palette-write helper at 0x2f240 starting at hardware colour index 0xf0/0xf5/0xf6/0xf8.
Evidence: No Function ID hits at all. The body is a large game-specific switch over the screen id at 0x00069cf4 with hand-written cases for ids 0x00,0x02,0x08,0x14,0x15,0x16,0x17,0x1a,0x1c,0x1d, each with its own cycle period (0x14,0x3c,0x24,0x1c,0x2c,0x28) and its own set of rodata colour tables at 0x2b2a0-0x2b4cd inlined via REP MOVSD. It reads/writes the game's tick globals 0x00069d20 / 0x00069d64 / 0x00069d24 and calls fdps_cd_music_repeat_poll (0x30c50). Callers are named game functions (fdps_render_view_frame, fdps_menu_cursor_input_loop, fdps_prompt_two_choice). Nothing here resembles a CLIB3S/MATH387S/EMU387 routine, there is no interrupt or driver-structure access that would suggest Miles AIL, and it is far too large and data-specific to be a linker thunk or compiler helper. Existing pool_fdps/subsys_graphics tags from the backbone walk agree.

=== 0002f2f0 [PLATE]
Strided rectangular block transfer for framebuffer/surface memory.

Algorithm:
Two modes selected by src_stride. When src_stride is zero the routine runs in fill mode: it treats src_or_fill as a byte value and calls memset(dst, src_or_fill, bytes_per_row) once per row, advancing dst by dst_stride after each row. When src_stride is non-zero it runs in copy mode: it calls memmove(dst, src, bytes_per_row) once per row, advancing src by src_stride and dst by dst_stride after each row. Both modes loop exactly rows times with a signed comparison, so a rows value of zero or less transfers nothing. No clipping, no bounds check and no transparency test is performed; the caller is responsible for the geometry. The row counter is kept in a stack local and the working src/dst cursors are stack copies of the incoming pointers, so the caller's values are not disturbed.

Parameters:
  src_or_fill  - in copy mode the source base pointer; in fill mode the byte value used to fill every row (only the low 8 bits reach memset)
  src_stride   - bytes added to the source cursor per row; zero selects fill mode

=== 0002fb80 [PLATE]
Mosaic screen transition: copies the source surface to the destination in block-sized rectangles, visiting them in a shuffled order so the image appears in random patches.

Algorithm:
1. Allocates grid_cols*grid_rows entries of 4 bytes (two int16 fields: column, row) via the CRT allocator and fills it with every (col,row) pair of the phase grid.
2. Shuffles the table in place: for every index i it draws two rand() values and forms j = rand()%grid_cols + grid_cols*(rand()%grid_rows), then swaps entry i with entry j. This is a random-swap shuffle, not a Fisher-Yates pass.
3. Computes the block counts: blocks_x = ceil((width/block_w)/grid_cols), blocks_y = ceil((height/block_h)/grid_rows). Each shuffled entry therefore owns a lattice of blocks spaced grid_cols apart.
4. For each shuffled entry (bx,by), walks that lattice. Row index is y = block_h*(j*grid_cols + by); column index is x = bx + i*grid_cols. A block is drawn only when x < width and y < height. Source address is src + y*src_pitch + x*block_w; destination address is dst + y*dst_pitch + (dst_pitch ? x*block_w : 0). Each block is handed to fdps_blit_rect with block_w by block_h.
5. After finishing one shuffled entry it calls the delay/present thunk at 0003d370 with the delay argument, so one entry of the table equals one visible step of the transition.
6. Frees the table before returning.

Note the bound test on the horizontal axis compares a block-column index against the pixel width, while the vertical test compares a pixel row against the pixel height. The horizontal test is therefore far looser than the vertical one; the real bound comes from the blocks_x loop count.

Parameters:
  dst        destination surface base address
  dst_pitch  destination bytes per row; zero suppresses the horizontal destination offset entirely
  src        source surface base address
  src_pitch  source bytes per row
  width      source width in pixels
  height     source height in pixels
  grid_cols  number of phase columns; also the horizontal stride between blocks of one phase
  grid_rows  number of phase rows
  block_w    block width in pixels
  block_h    block height in pixels
  delay      value passed to the per-step delay/present thunk at 0003d370

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps
Builds a malloc'd array of every (col,row) block index of a screen grid, Fisher-Yates shuffles it with the game's rand helper, then blits the source image block by block in that random order with a per-row wait, freeing the array at the end.
Evidence: Disassembly is plain application logic: it fills a 4-byte-per-entry table of 16-bit x/y block coordinates, shuffles it with two calls to the game rand at 0x42cf8, computes block pixel sizes from the caller's stride/width/height arguments, and calls fdps_blit_rect (0x2f2f0) for each visible block, then a per-block-row delay thunk at 0x3d370. Its only library calls are crt_malloc and crt_free, which is the usage pattern of game code, not of runtime code. Both callers are game-side screen code (fdps_load_game_screen and FUN_000241e0). No Function ID hits at all, and nothing here resembles a CRT, math, 80x87-emulator or Miles AIL routine: no DOS interrupt path, no driver structure, no 0x70000 state area. Far too large and too parameterised (six-plus stack args, nested loops) to be a linker thunk or compiler helper, so not binary_artifact.

=== 00030010 [PLATE]
Alpha-blends a single constant palette colour over an 8bpp source rectangle.

Algorithm:
blend_table is a [18][256] array of dwords holding each palette entry pre-scaled by a weight, with the three colour channels packed one per byte (channel n in bits 8n+4..8n+7 before the shift below). Rows 0..8 hold weights 0..8; rows 9..17 (dword offset 0x900 = 9*256) hold the complementary weights. To keep the row index inside 0..8 the function folds alpha: for alpha <= 8 the constant colour reads row alpha and the source pixels read row 9+alpha; for alpha > 8 alpha is replaced by 16-alpha, the constant colour reads row 9+alpha' and the source pixels read row alpha'. Either way the constant colour ends up weighted by the caller's alpha and the source pixel by 16-alpha.
The scaled constant colour is fetched once before the loops. For each pixel the scaled source colour is added to it, the sum is shifted right by 4 (dividing out the /16 of the weights) and masked with 0x000F0F0F, leaving 4 bits per channel at bits 0..3, 8..11 and 16..19. Those are folded into a 12-bit index by (v & 0xFFFF) | (v >> 12), giving channel0 in bits 0..3, channel2 in bits 4..7 and channel1 in bits 8..11. That index selects a palette byte from the 4096-entry inverse-palette table rgb444_lut, which is stored to the destination.
Rows advance by src_stride and dst_stride; no clipping, no transparency test, every pixel in the rectangle is written.

Parameters:
src         - source 8bpp pixels, top-left of the rectangle
src_stride  - bytes to add to src per row
dst         - destination 8bpp pixels, top-left of the rectangle
dst_stride  - bytes to add to dst per row
width       - pixels per row
height      - number of rows
blend_table - base of the [18][256] dword weighted-colour table
rgb444_lut  - base of the 4096-entry packed-RGB to palette-index table
tint_color  - palette index of the constant colour being blended in
alpha       - blend weight of tint_color, 0..16 (0 = source only, 16 = tint only)

Returns:
Nothing.

Pool: fdps
Per-pixel cross-fade/tint blitter: for each row and column of a rect it reads a source palette index, looks up two packed 0x0f0f0f RGB entries from a 0x900-stride table pair selected by a fade step (0..16), averages them with SAR 4, repacks the result into a 16-bit key and uses it to index an inverse-colour lookup table, storing the resulting index to the destination scanline.
Evidence: Plain __cdecl stack-frame routine taking nine stack arguments (source ptr, source stride, dest ptr, dest stride, width, height, table base, inverse-LUT base, fade step) and touching no globals, no interrupts, no DOS/driver state and no CRT helpers - it calls nothing at all. The arithmetic is game-specific 8-bit palette blending against a fade-ramp table indexed by a step clamped around 8/16, which corresponds to no CLIB3S/MATH387S/EMU387 entry, and fid returned zero hits. === 00030790 [PLATE]
Periodic timer tick callback.

Algorithm: Increments the global 32-bit tick counter at 00069d64, then calls the per-tick service routine FUN_00042cf8 and returns. The tick counter is read (never written) by roughly fifty game functions -- title screen, game over, view rendering, and many battle/menu routines -- which sample it to build delay and frame-pacing loops, so this handler is the single writer that makes those loops advance. The function's address is taken and passed to fdps_audio_timer_install (address reference at 000307bc, stored at 000307c1), which is the only reference to it: nothing calls it directly, it is invoked from the installed timer hook. The body touches no parameters and no registers beyond the standard PUSH ESI/EDI/EBP frame; the SUB ESP,0x0 is Watcom's empty-locals prologue.

Parameters: None.

Returns: Nothing.

=== 000307b0 [PLATE]
Installs and starts the audio service timer.

Algorithm:
  1. Calls the timer-registration routine FUN_0003e196 with the address of the
     tick callback FUN_00030790 (which bumps the counter at 0x00069d64 and then
     calls the audio service routine FUN_00042cf8). The returned timer handle is
     stored in the global at 0x00069d50.
  2. If the handle is -1 the registration failed; the fatal/report routine
     FUN_00042deb is called with the literal " Timer fail !!!\n" at 0x00061ea8.
     Execution is not stopped locally - the function falls through regardless.
  3. Calls FUN_0003e3ea(handle, rate) to program the timer with the rate value
     passed in by the caller.
  4. Calls FUN_0003e5b3(handle) to start the timer.

All three timer routines are reached with arguments pushed on the stack and the
caller cleaning up (ADD ESP,n after each CALL), i.e. the vendor sound library's
stack convention.

Parameters:
  rate - timer rate/period value handed straight to the timer programming call;
         the only stack slot this function reads ([EBP+0x14]).

Returns:
  Nothing. The timer handle is left in the global at 0x00069d50 for later use.

Pool: fdps
Registers the game's audio timer callback (0x00030790) through the AIL timer API, aborts with the game error printer if registration fails, then sets the timer period from its argument and starts the timer.
Evidence: Disassembly is application-side glue over three AIL entry points (0x0003e196 register_timer returning -1 on failure, 0x0003e3ea set_timer_period, 0x0003e5b3 start_timer), not a library routine itself: it composes them, stores the handle in the game global 0x00069d50, and passes its own callback address 0x00030790, which sits in the same code cluster as its only caller fdps_audio_init@000304e0. === 00030c50 [PLATE]
Periodic CD background-music keep-alive, polled from the game loops.

Algorithm:
  Compares the cached tick value at 0x00069d74 with the live timer tick at
  0x00069d64 and returns immediately when they are equal, so the body runs at
  most once per timer tick regardless of how often the caller polls.
  On a new tick it increments the tick accumulator at 0x00060170. When the
  accumulator reaches 0x4b (75 ticks) it performs the actual check: if a track
  is selected (0x00069d54 != -1) and the CD audio enable flag at 0x00060008 is
  non-zero, it queries playback state via FUN_0003c6e8; a non-zero 16-bit
  result means the track is no longer playing, in which case FUN_0003c85b is
  called with (track index + 1) to start the track again. The accumulator is
  then reset to zero. Finally the cached tick is refreshed from the live tick.
  The selected-track global holds a zero-based index; the play routine takes a
  one-based CD track number, hence the +1.

Parameters:
  None. All state is read from and written to globals.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Pool: fdps
Per-frame CD music watchdog: once the frame counter at 0x00069d64 advances, it increments a counter at 0x00060170 and every 75 ticks checks whether the current CD track (0x00069d54, -1 meaning none) and the audio-enabled flag at 0x00060008 are valid and the CD drive is idle, and if so restarts playback of that track via fdps_cd_play_track.
Evidence: The body is pure game state polling: it reads and writes four game globals (frame tick 0x00069d64, last-seen tick 0x00069d74, retry counter 0x00060170, current track 0x00069d54, audio flag 0x00060008), applies a game-specific magic period of 0x4b ticks, and its only two callees are the already-classified fdps CD helpers fdps_cd_audio_is_idle and fdps_cd_play_track. It is called from eight game loops (battle player phase, palette cycling, map cursor select, village signboard menu, and four unnamed scene loops), never from crt_ or AIL_ code. The fid list is empty, so no Watcom library match exists; no CRT prologue/helper pattern, no DOS interrupt or .DIG driver structure access, and it is far too substantial to be a linker thunk or jump island.

=== 00030cc0 [PLATE]
Verify the correct game CD is inserted for a chapter, then start its CD audio track.

Algorithm:
1. Copy a 60-byte constant table from 000304a0 onto the stack. It is 30 chapter rows of 2 bytes; the row is the chapter, the column is the track slot, and the byte is a zero-based CD audio track index.
2. Stop any playing CD audio (fdps_cd_stop_audio at 0003c4a7).
3. Loop until the inserted disc is acceptable:
   - Uninstall the keyboard ISR (00056818) and drain pending input (00043570 / 00043587).
   - Build "%s\\Pack.vfs" from the CD-ROM root path global at 000643c4 (00042d41) and probe it (00042438). A non-zero result means the archive could not be opened, i.e. no usable disc.
   - On success, load the "Pass.Dat" entry through fdps_vfs_load_entry and take its first byte minus '0' as the disc number (1 or 2).
   - Chapters 0..17 live on disc 1, chapters 18 (0x12) and above on disc 2. If the probe failed, or the disc number does not match the chapter, draw the matching prompt string (message id 0x223 for "insert disc 2", 0x222 for "insert disc 1", followed by id 0x22a) via 0001ff60 at 320x208, wait 20000 ticks (0003d370), tear the prompt down (00020820) and retry.
   - Otherwise set the done flag and leave the loop.
4. Reinstall the keyboard ISR (fdps_install_keyboard_isr).
5. If the CD audio enable flag at 00060008 is clear, store -1 into the current-track global at 00069d54 and stop CD audio. Otherwise read table[chapter * 2 + slot], store it at 00069d54, and start playback of track value + 1 (0003c85b).

Parameters:
  chapter - chapter index, 0..29; also selects the required disc (>= 18 means disc 2).
  slot    - which of the chapter's two track entries to play, 0 or 1.

Returns:
  Nothing. Does not return until an acceptable disc is present.

Pool: fdps
Copies a 60-byte per-chapter CD track table onto the stack, loops asking the player to insert the correct FDPS disc (identified by a digit read from a VFS entry) while drawing prompt strings and stopping CD audio, then selects the track for the current chapter/slot and starts CD playback or stops audio if there is none.
Evidence: Disassembly is pure game logic: an inline 60-byte table copied from 0x304a0 indexed by [ebp+0x14] (chapter) and [ebp+0x18], a disc-swap prompt loop that calls fdps_vfs_load_entry to read a disc-id character and subtracts '0', two 7-argument text/sprite draw calls through FUN_0001ff60 with game resource pointers (0xaa44a, 0xabc0a) and the global screen context at 0x643c4, a delay of 0x4e20, and finally fdps_cd_play_track / fdps_cd_stop_audio on the global current-track variable at 0x69d54. All four callers are already-named game functions (battle turn advance, options menu, savegame load, village phase). No Function ID hits at all, no CRT idioms, no Miles AIL driver structures or 0x70000 state area, no INT dispatch of its own. Not binary_artifact: 626 bytes of real control flow with a normal Watcom stack frame.

=== 00031210 [PLATE]
Runs the village phase between chapters.

Algorithm:

2. Test the current chapter number at 0x00069cf4. Returns: the menu selection left over when the loop exited, which is 0 on a normal exit and 0 when the abort flag was already set on entry.

=== 00031540 [PLATE]
