=== 00031bc0 [PLATE]
Village signboard menu loop.

Algorithm:
1. Copies three 9-byte VGA DAC ramp tables (R at 0x31064, G at 0x3106d, B at 0x31076) into locals; they drive the pulsing highlight colour.
2. Clamps the global scene index at 0x000601a4 against the count at 0x00064114, then loads the signboard cel "CanBan.cel" from the "MISC_VFS" archive (FUN_0002a140). The handle is freed on exit.
3. Each iteration: draws the village backdrop (FUN_00030c50), reads a keyboard scancode (FUN_000567be, masked to 8 bits). Scancodes >= 0x7F are ignored. FUN_000357a0 acts as a hotkey/abort filter: when it returns non-zero the selection is forced to 5 and the selection-change handler FUN_00031f60 runs.
   - 0x4B (left) / 0x48 (up): plays "Beep.wav" (FUN_0002a1f0), selection = (selection + 4) % 5, calls FUN_00031f60.
   - 0x4D (right) / 0x50 (down): plays "Beep.wav", selection = (selection + 1) % 5, calls FUN_00031f60.
   - 0x1C (Enter) / 0x39 (Space): sets the exit flag.
   - 0x0F (Tab): advances the scene index at 0x000601a4 modulo the count at 0x00064114.
4. Picks an animation cell from the frame counter (frame/5 & 3, with 3 folded back to 1), resolves the sprite through the table at 0x00060138 offset by scene index * 0x30, allocates a 64000-byte off-screen page (FUN_0003d375) and fills it with the caller-supplied background image (FUN_0003d514, 320x200).
5. Blits the animated figure (FUN_000568db) at the position given by the x table at 0x00060174 and the y table at 0x0006018C indexed by the current selection, then draws the signboard text twice through FUN_0002dba0 (once for entry 6, once for the current selection, i.e. the highlighted line).
6. Waits for vertical retrace on port 0x3DA (bit 3), then writes DAC entries 0xF0..0xF4 through ports 0x3C8/0x3C9 using the ramp tables phase-shifted by (frame/3) % 5, waits for retrace to end, copies the off-screen page to 0xA0000, spins until the timer tick at 0x00069D64 changes, and frees the page.

Parameters:
  background - pointer to a 64000-byte (320x200) background image copied into the off-screen page every frame.
  selection  - in/out pointer to the current menu selection (0..4, or 5 when the hotkey filter fires); updated in place and read by the caller after return.

Returns:
  Nothing. The cel handle and the off-screen page are released before returning.

Pool: fdps

=== 00036b60 [PLATE]
Sets the low nibble of the byte at offset 0x34 for every record in a closed index range of the global 0x50-byte object table.

Algorithm:
  i = first_index
  while (i <= last_index) {
      rec = object_at(i);            /* FUN_0002d210: *(char**)0x00069cd8 + i * 0x50 */
      rec[0x34] = (rec[0x34] & 0xF0) | value;
  }
  The high nibble of rec[0x34] is preserved; only the low nibble is replaced.
  The loop is inclusive of last_index, so first_index == last_index touches exactly
  one record. If first_index > last_index nothing is written.
  All three observed call sites pass value = 0, i.e. they clear the low nibble.
  Only the low byte of the third stack slot is read (register DH).

Parameters:
  [EBP+0x14] int first_index  - first object index, inclusive
  [EBP+0x18] int last_index   - last object index, inclusive
  [EBP+0x1C] unsigned char value - value merged into the low nibble of field 0x34

Returns:
  Nothing. Arguments are passed on the stack and removed by the caller (ADD ESP,0xC).

=== 00039ab0 [PLATE]
Opens a VFS container and builds its in-memory directory handle.

Algorithm:
  1. fopen(path, "rb"). Return NULL if it fails.
  2. fseek to offset 7, fread a u32 entry_count.
  3. fseek to offset 5, fread a u16 table_offset (later sign-extended when used as a seek target, so the usable range is 0..0x7FFF).
  4. Allocate 0x11 + entry_count * 0x1A bytes for the handle. If the allocation fails, still close the file and return NULL.
  5. memset the first 0x11 bytes of the handle to zero, store entry_count at offset 0, and memcpy strlen(path) bytes of the container path to offset 4 (the zeroed header leaves it NUL terminated for names up to 12 characters).
  6. fseek to table_offset and fread entry_count entries of 0x1A bytes each into handle+0x11.
  7. fclose and return the handle.

The container magic "VFS", the version word, the 24-byte signature, the duplicated per-entry size and the reserved byte are never examined, so a non-VFS file is not rejected here.

Parameters:
  path - NUL terminated container file name, opened through the C runtime, no directory search of its own.

Returns:
  Pointer to the allocated container handle {u32 entry_count; char path[13]; entry table of entry_count * 0x1A bytes}, or NULL if the file could not be opened or the handle could not be allocated.

Pool: fdps
Opens a game archive file, reads its entry count and header fields, allocates a directory structure of count*0x1a+0x11 bytes, copies the archive filename into it, loads the entry table from the file, closes the file and returns the handle.
Evidence: Disassembly is application-level archive/VFS logic, not runtime: it fopen()s a path passed as a parameter with a mode string at 0x6201c, fseek/fread's a 4-byte entry count at offset 7 and a 2-byte field at offset 5, computes a game-specific record size (0x1a bytes per entry plus a 0x11-byte header), calls crt_malloc for it, memsets, strlen/strcpy's the filename into the block, then bulk-reads the entry table and fcloses. === 0003bade [PLATE]
Allocates the DOS real-mode communication buffers used by the CD-ROM (MSCDEX) driver layer.

Algorithm:
1. Zero the 12-byte struct SREGS at 0x00069df0 with memset.
2. Fill the input REGS at 0x00069dc8 with AX = 0x0100 and BX = 0x0020, then call int386x(0x31, in, out, sregs). DPMI function 0100h allocates 0x20 paragraphs (512 bytes) of DOS memory below 1MB; the returned AX is the real-mode segment and DX the protected-mode selector (the selector is discarded).
3. Store the first block's real-mode segment as a word at 0x00069e54 and its flat linear address (segment << 4) at 0x00069de8. Under DOS/4GW the first megabyte is identity mapped, so segment << 4 is directly dereferenceable.
4. Repeat the identical DPMI 0100h call for a second 512-byte block; store its segment shifted left 16 bits at 0x00069da8 (pre-packed seg:0000 real-mode far pointer for the MSCDEX request header transfer address field) and its flat linear address (segment << 4) at 0x00069da4.

The input REGS block is not re-initialised before the second call because int386x leaves the caller's input structure untouched.

No error handling: a failed DPMI allocation leaves the carry flag set and garbage in AX, and the resulting addresses are used unchecked by the CD driver functions.

Parameters: none.

Returns: nothing. Results are published through the globals at 0x00069da4, 0x00069da8, 0x00069de8 and 0x00069e54.

Pool: fdps
Allocates two DOS real-mode memory blocks via DPMI INT 31h function 0x100 (0x20 paragraphs each) and records their segment and linear addresses in the globals used by the CD-ROM/MSCDEX path.
Evidence: Disassembly builds a DPMI register block at 0x69dc8 (EAX=0x100 allocate DOS memory, EBX=0x20 paragraphs), zeroes it with a memset-like call, then invokes the INT 0x31 simulation helper at 0x43657 twice, converting the returned real-mode segment at 0x69dac into segment:offset and linear forms stored at 0x69e54/0x69de8/0x69da8/0x69da4. This is application-level buffer setup for the game's own CD detection, not library code: it is called only by fdps_cdrom_detect, it writes game-owned globals in the 0x69dxx block, and no Watcom or DOS/4G library routine allocates into these specific game globals. The fid list is empty, so there is no CRT match; the only CRT contact is the callee at 0x4361a, the Watcom stack-probe with its 0x14 frame size, which appears in ordinary compiled game functions. Nothing touches the AIL driver structures or the 0x70000 state area, so it is not ail; it is a full compiled C function with a real frame, not a thunk or jump island, so it is not binary_artifact.

=== 0003bb7d [PLATE]
Sends the currently prepared MSCDEX request header to the CD-ROM device driver.

Algorithm:
Clears the SREGS block at 0x00069df0 (12 bytes) and the DPMI real-mode call structure at 0x00069e22 (0x32 bytes). Fills the real-mode structure with EAX=0x1510 (MSCDEX Send Device Request), ECX = the CD-ROM subunit number held in the byte at 0x00069dfe, EBX=0 and ES = the real-mode segment of the request header held in the word at 0x00069e54, so that the driver receives ES:BX pointing at the request header. It then fills the protected-mode input REGS block at 0x00069dc8 with EAX=0x0300 (DPMI Simulate Real Mode Interrupt), BL=0x2f (interrupt 2Fh), BH=0, ECX=0 (no words copied from the protected-mode stack) and EDI = 0x00069e22, sets SREGS.es to DS, and calls int86x(0x31, &inregs, &outregs, &sregs). If the carry flag in the output REGS (0x00069dc4) is set, it prints "DEVICE REQUEST FAILED!!!" and returns anyway; the MSCDEX status word in the request header is not inspected here.

Parameters:
None. Every input is a file-scope global: the request header itself and its real-mode segment at 0x00069e54, and the CD-ROM subunit number at 0x00069dfe. Callers fill the request header before calling.

Returns:
Nothing. Failure is only reported on stdout; the caller must read the request header status field itself.

Pool: fdps
Builds an MSCDEX device request header and command block in the game's CD state area, then issues real-mode INT 2Fh AX=1510h (send device request) through the DPMI simulate-interrupt helper, reporting an error string if the driver reports failure.
Evidence: Disassembly is game-specific driver glue: it zero-fills two globals at 0x69df0/0x69e22, stores AX=0x1510 into a real-mode register image, fills an MSCDEX request header (subunit/command 0x2f, length fields) and passes it to the DPMI int-simulation helper with interrupt number 0x31. No fid hits at all, and no CRT/math/x87 behaviour. Callees are the shared memset-like helper (00042cd0), an error/print helper (00042deb), a Watcom stack-probe (0004361a) and the DPMI interrupt helper (00043657) -- all generic, none identifying. All 13 callers are the surrounding CD-ROM cluster at 0x3b-0x3c, two of which are already named fdps_cdrom_read_disk_info and fdps_cd_stop_audio, so this is the shared request primitive of the game's own CD subsystem. Not AIL: it touches the MSCDEX/INT 2Fh path and the 0x69dxx CD state block, not the .DIG driver structures or the 0x70000 AIL state area, and no AIL routine calls it. Existing backbone tags pool_fdps/subsys_cd agree.

Pool: fdps

=== 0003c636 [PLATE]
CD-ROM presence check, called once from main during startup. main sign-extends the
result and aborts with "Fatal error: CDROM is not install!!!" unless it is exactly 1.

Algorithm:
  1. PUSH 0x10 / CALL __CHK (0004361a) - Watcom stack probe for the 16 bytes this call
     chain needs. Not a parameter.
  2. Fills the input union REGS at 00069dc8: AL=0 (00069dc8), AH=0x15 (00069dc9),
     BX=0 (00069dcc), i.e. AX=1500h - the MSCDEX installation check.
  3. int386(0x2f, &in_regs at 00069dc8, &out_regs at 00069dac) via 00043268.
     On return the output block holds BX at 00069db0 (number of CD-ROM drive letters)
     and CX at 00069db4 (index of the first CD-ROM drive letter, 0 = A:).
  4. If BX == 0 no CD-ROM redirector is loaded: return 0 immediately.
  5. Otherwise publishes the result to the CD subsystem globals: the drive count word
     goes to 00069dfc and the low byte of the first-drive-letter index to 00069dfe.
  6. If the flag at 00069e54 is still zero, calls the one-time CD initialiser at
     0003bade, then always calls 0003bfa5, which leaves a 16-bit status word at
     00069e20.
  7. Returns 2 if that status word is 0x810C, otherwise 1.

Parameters:
  None. The decompiler's param_1/param_2/unaff_EBX are artifacts: param_1 is the
  0x10 stack-probe immediate, and nothing in the body reads an incoming register or
  a stack slot.

Returns:
  0 - no MSCDEX / CD-ROM redirector installed (INT 2Fh AX=1500h returned BX=0).
  1 - CD-ROM found and the device request completed with a status other than 0x810C.
  2 - CD-ROM found but the device request left status 0x810C at 00069e20.
  Only 1 is accepted by main; both 0 and 2 end the program.

Pool: fdps
Detects the game CD by issuing the MSCDEX INT 2Fh AX=1500h drive-list call, and when a drive is present records the drive letter/count, allocates the DOS transfer buffers, reads the disc info and returns 2 for the disc whose id equals 0x810C, 1 otherwise, or 0 when no CD-ROM driver is present.

The entry PUSH 0x10 / CALL 0x0004361a is the Watcom stack-check prologue (__STK), which marks this as compiler-generated Watcom C application code, not a hand-written thunk; the callee is CRT, this function is not. === 0003c984 [PLATE]
Pool: ail
Fetches len bytes of an LX module at a given file offset for the driver-image loader: when bit 0 of the flags argument is set the image is already resident and it memcpy's from base+offset, otherwise it lseek(handle, offset, SEEK_SET) then read(handle, dest, len); returns offset+len as the new position so the caller can walk the header, object table and fixup records sequentially.
Evidence: Both callers, and the only callers in the image, are FUN_0003cbc1 and FUN_0003ccf8, which have now been judged ail: they are the two halves of the Miles AIL .DIG/.MDI driver loader (the sizing pass and the load+relocate pass), both parsing the LX header at e_lfanew, the "LX" magic at 0x00062258, the 0x18-byte object table and the fixup page table. This function is the read primitive those two passes are built on -- every structure they parse is obtained through it, and the flags bit selecting 'copy from an already-resident image' versus 'seek and read from the handle' is exactly the dual-source access an embeddable module loader needs. A helper whose entire caller set is ail is ail. The three callees (0x435bc crt_memcpy, 0x43694 crt_lseek, 0x436df crt_read) are all confirmed CLIB3S primitives, which places this function one layer above the CRT, consuming it rather than belonging to it; the empty FID result confirms it is no CLIB3S/MATH387S/EMU387 routine itself. Not fdps: the game's own resource paths do not reach it, and it exists only to serve the LX loader. Not binary_artifact: 87 bytes of real branching logic with five stack arguments and caller cleanup. The prologue anomaly noted on the first pass now reads as supporting evidence rather than a puzzle -- pushing only ESI/EDI/EBP while treating EBX as scratch, with cdecl stack arguments, is not the project's wcc386 -4s -od shape, which is what a third-party vendor object compiled with its own flags looks like, and AIL is exactly such a vendor library. As with its two callers, the upstream Miles symbol is not identified, so no AIL_ name is proposed.

Miles Sound System AIL API entry point: AIL_shutdown().

Algorithm:
The function is the standard Miles API wrapper generated for every public AIL
entry point. It increments the global API nesting depth counter at 0x00069e6c
on entry and decrements it on exit. If the debug log is enabled (0x00069e80

which takes no arguments. Afterwards the same log-enable test is repeated and,
if it passes, the log stream at 0x00069e7c is flushed through 0x000428be.
The function has no early exits and always falls through to the depth decrement.

Parameters:
None.

Returns:
Nothing.

=== 00042e0f [PLATE]
C runtime exit().

Algorithm:
  Calls two runtime finalizer hooks indirectly through the function-pointer
  slots at 0x000603a0 and 0x000603a4, then pushes its own status argument and
  calls the next termination stage at 0x00042e29 (_exit), cleaning the argument
  off the stack afterwards.

  The three adjacent slots 0x000603a0 / 0x000603a4 / 0x000603a8 form the
  runtime's finalizer hook table. exit() runs slots [0] and [1]; the _exit
  stage at 0x00042e29 runs slots [1] and [2] and then jumps into the cstart
  termination tail at 0x00043527, which pops the status into EAX and reaches
  INT 21h AH=4Ch. In this build all three slots are statically initialised to
  0x00042e0e, a bare RET stub, i.e. no finalizer module was linked in, so the
  hooks are effectively no-ops.

  The trailing RET is unreachable: control never comes back from 0x00042e29.
  This function does not return.

Parameters:
  [ESP+4]  int status - process exit code, forwarded unchanged to _exit and
           ultimately to the DOS terminate call.

Returns:
  Does not return.

=== 00043298 [PLATE]
LE module entry point (Watcom cstart_.asm).

Algorithm:
  The whole body is one 2-byte instruction, JMP 0x00043310 (EB 76). The 0x76
  bytes it jumps over are data, not code: the ASCII banner "WATCOM C/C++32
  Run-Time system. (c) Copyright by WATCOM International Corp. 1988-1994. All
  rights reserved." at 0004329A, a 3-byte LEA EAX,[EAX+0] pad, the runtime
  version/flag words 0003 0001, and the default console device name "con" at
  0004330C. Control lands on the startup body at 00043310, which begins
  STI / AND ESP,-4 / MOV EBX,ESP, identifies the DOS extender (RSX 'DX',
  'CB', or DPMI via INT 21h AX=FF00 'PHAR'), shrinks the DOS memory block,
  records PSP/environment pointers, copies the command tail, scans the
  environment for the "no87=" variable, clears BSS, runs the initialiser
  chain and finally exits through INT 21h AH=4Ch.

  This stub exists only so the entry address can sit immediately before the
  banner that the linker embeds; it is emitted by the Watcom startup object
  linked in by wlink and has no counterpart in hand-written C.

Parameters:
  None. Execution arrives here from the LE header's initial CS:EIP, set up by
  the DOS/4G loader; nothing is passed in registers or on the stack by any
  caller inside the image. Ghidra's six-parameter signature is an artifact of
  the decompiler inlining the jump target.

Returns:
  Does not return. The startup path it enters terminates the process with
  INT 21h AH=4Ch.

Pool: crt  [CLIB3S.LIB(_cstart_) -- identified by the embedded Watcom copyright banner, no FID hit]
Watcom C/C++ runtime startup entry point: a two-byte JMP that skips the inline copyright banner and lands on the real _cstart_ prologue at 0x00043310.
Evidence: The two bytes are EB 76 (JMP 0x00043310). The 0x76 bytes jumped over are the literal string 'WATCOM C/C++32 Run-Time system. (c) Copyright by WATCOM International Corp. 1988-1994. All rights reserved.' followed by the version words 03 00 01 00 and 'con'. The jump target 0x00043310 starts STI / AND ESP,0xFFFFFFFC / MOV EBX,ESP / MOV [..],EBX, the canonical Watcom _cstart_ prologue. This is the head of the library startup module itself, not a linker thunk: the banner is data emitted inside _cstart_ and the jump is _cstart_'s own first instruction, so it is crt rather than binary_artifact. === 00043310 [PLATE]
Named crt_cstart_body rather than crt_cstart because the LE entry symbol at
00043298 owns that name; the two are one piece of assembly separated only by
the banner data the linker embeds between them.

Watcom C/C++ 10.0a runtime startup code (cstrt386.asm, _cstart_). This is the
real program entry: the LE entry stub at 00043298 is a bare JMP to here. Hand
written assembly, not compiled C.

Algorithm:
  1. STI, align ESP down to a dword boundary, and record the initial stack
     pointer in the runtime globals at 00060434 and 00060420. Preload the
     default selector 0x24 into 0006042c and EBX with 'PHAR' for the Phar Lap
     probe.
  2. INT 21h AH=30h (get DOS version). AL/AH are stored as the DOS major and
     minor version at 00060457 and 00060458. The high half of EAX selects the
     host:
       - 'DX'  (0x4458): Phar Lap 386|DOS-Extender. Take the version digit from
         BL, read the PSP memory-block end at ES:[5Ch] via selector 0006042c,
         round it up to a 4K boundary, store it at 00060420 and shrink the
         block with INT 21h AH=4Ah. Environment selector 0x2C.
       - 'CB'  (0x4243): Intel Code Builder. EDX points at the Code Builder
         info block; it is saved at 000603ac. Shrink memory by the amount at
         [EDX+1Ch] (INT 21h AH=4Ah), take the PSP pointer from [EDX+10h] (the
         command tail therefore starts at PSP+81h) and the environment segment
         from [PSP+2Ch], shifted left by 4.
       - otherwise: INT 21h AX=FF00h with DX=78h. If it reports a host, this is
         a DPMI/DOS-4G style extender: the GS selector, when non-zero, is saved
         at 000603b0, INT 31h AX=0006h fetches the DS segment base, the PSP
         selector is taken from ES and the environment selector from ES:[2Ch].
         If it reports nothing, fall back to the fixed real-mode-ish selectors
         (PSP 0x24, environment 0x2C, flat data 0x17).
     The resulting host type/subtype byte pair is written to 0006044e/0006044f,
     the environment pointer to 00060451 and its selector to 00060455.
  3. Self-modifying step: with the flat data selector in ES, store DS into the
     code at 0004356d, which is the operand of the "MOV DS,CS:[4356Dh]"
     instruction in the exit path at 00043564.
  4. Command line: read the tail length from PSP:80h, skip leading spaces with
     REPE SCASB, and copy the remaining tail with REP MOVSB to the 16-byte
     aligned buffer just past the end of BSS (0006a3bc rounded up), then append
     two NUL bytes. The buffer address is kept in 00060428.
  5. Environment scan: walk the environment strings; a string whose first four
     bytes lowercase to "no87" and whose fifth byte is '=' increments the
     no-x87 flag stored at 0006044c. After the terminating double NUL, skip the
     word count and copy the program name that follows to the end of the
     command line buffer; the pointer past it is stored at 00060430. The stack
     pointer is also recorded at 0006041c.
  6. Zero BSS from 00063930 up to 0006a3bc with REP STOSD plus a byte tail.
     When the host type byte at 0006044e is 1 (the DPMI path, where the loader
     already zero-fills the image) the cleared span is clamped to 0x1000 bytes.
     The aligned end of BSS is then stored at 00060424 as the heap/break base.
  7. Call __InitRtns (0004dfa6) with EAX=0FFh to run every registered
     initializer up to priority 255, clear EBP, then call __CMain (0004df4c),
     which sets up the stack limit, builds argc/argv and calls main (00029220),
     then exit (00042e0f). __CMain therefore never returns; the POP EAX / JMP
     00043528 tail that follows it only executes on paths that reach the shared
     exit sequence at 0004354d, which runs __FiniRtns (0004dff1) with
     EAX=0, EDX=0FFh and terminates with INT 21h AH=4Ch.

Parameters: none at the C level. The only incoming register state that is read
is supplied by the extender/loader: EDX (Intel Code Builder info block) and GS
(DPMI). The incoming stack contents are not used; ESP is only realigned and
recorded.

Returns: never returns. Control leaves through main/exit inside __CMain, or
through the INT 21h AH=4Ch terminate in the shared exit tail at 0004354d.

Pool: crt
Watcom 32-bit DOS startup body: identifies the DOS extender (INT 21h/30h, 'PHAR'/DX/CB signatures, INT 31h DPMI), shrinks the DOS memory block, copies the PSP command tail and environment, records NO87, zeroes BSS, then calls __InitRtns and __CMain.
Evidence: Pure CSTRT386.ASM-shape startup assembly with no C prologue: STI, AND ESP,-4, raw INT 21h AH=30h/4Ah, INT 31h AX=0006, segment-register juggling and REP MOVSB/STOSD over the low-memory globals at 0x6041c-0x60458, ending in CALL 0004dfa6 (crt_init_rtns) and CALL 0004df4c (crt_cmain). It has zero callers because it is the module entry path, and the only things it calls are named CRT routines, so it is runtime, not game logic. Not ail (no .DIG driver structures, no 0x70000 state area) and not binary_artifact (538 bytes of real startup work, not a thunk). No fid hit because Watcom's startup lives in the linker-supplied startup object, which the Function ID library does not cover.
Open question: Whether this address is the true entry symbol _cstart_ or the continuation body after the 386-check stub; leaving the name unproposed rather than guessing crt__cstart_.

=== 000435a2 [PLATE]
Watcom CRT variadic formatting entry point (sprintf).

Algorithm:
Preserves EBX, then rebuilds a three-argument stack frame for the internal
worker at 0004e1e9: it computes LEA EAX,[ESP+0x10], which is the address of
the first variadic slot on the caller's stack (a va_list), and pushes it last
of the three so the worker receives (dest, format, va_list) in cdecl order.
The first two incoming stack arguments are re-pushed unchanged. After the
call the wrapper removes the 12 bytes it pushed (ADD ESP,0xc), restores EBX
and returns; EAX is left untouched, so the worker's return value is the
return value of this function. 0004e1e9 in turn appends a global pointer read
from 00061454 and calls the formatting engine at 00054dc7. All three
functions in that chain have exactly one caller each, and the only caller of
this wrapper is fdps_play_movie at 00030f40, so the whole formatting chain was
linked in for a single call site.

Parameters:
  arg1 (stack, [ESP+8] at entry) - destination buffer receiving the formatted
    text.
  arg2 (stack, [ESP+0xc] at entry) - format string.
  ... (stack, from [ESP+0x10] at entry) - variadic arguments consumed by the
    conversion specifiers; their address is passed on as a va_list.

Returns:
  int, propagated unchanged from the worker (character count in the CRT
  contract).

Pool: crt  [CLIB3S.LIB(sprintf); FID only offered spawnlp score 26.68 (rejected, same varargs-wrapper shape)]

Evidence: Disassembly is the canonical Watcom varargs wrapper: PUSH EBX; LEA EAX,[ESP+0x10] (address of the first stack vararg); PUSH EAX; PUSH [fmt]; PUSH [buf]; CALL 0004e1e9; ADD ESP,0xc (cdecl, caller cleans). The callee 0004e1e9 is itself a thin forwarder that re-pushes those three arguments plus a fourth loaded from the global at 00061454 and calls the shared formatting engine at ~00054db0 -- the vsprintf/__vbprintf shape of the printf family. === 00043c82 [PLATE]
Watcom C runtime initialiser: calibrate the delay() busy-wait loop.

Algorithm:
  Phase 1 (sync): issue DOS "Get System Time" (INT 21h, AH=2Ch; returns
  CH=hour, CL=minute, DH=second, DL=hundredths), keep the seconds field
  (DH), then re-issue the call until DH changes. This aligns the
  measurement with a whole-second boundary so no partial second is
  counted.
  Phase 2 (count): with the new seconds value latched in BL, spin issuing
  INT 21h AH=2Ch and incrementing a counter until DH changes again. The
  counter therefore holds the number of INT 21h AH=2Ch round trips this
  machine performs in one second.
  The result is stored to the global at 0x00069ea8. delay() at 0x00043cb0
  is its only consumer: it computes
  iterations = (milliseconds * [0x00069ea8] + 500) / 1000, clamps a zero
  result up to 1, and spins that many INT 21h AH=2Ch calls. The stored
  value is thus "loop iterations per 1000 ms" on the host CPU.

  The routine is not reached by a CALL. It is entry 0 of the Watcom
  runtime init table at 0x000638f0 (6-byte records: status byte,
  priority byte, 32-bit routine address); its record reads
  00 20 82 3C 04 00 - status 0 (pending), priority 0x20
  (INIT_PRIORITY_LIBRARY), routine 0x00043C82. The table walker at
  0x0004DFA6 invokes it during startup and then marks the record 2 (done).

Parameters:
  None. EBX and ESI are pushed on entry and popped on exit; every other
  register the body reads (EAX, EDX) is written by INT 21h before being
  used, so no incoming register or stack argument exists.

Returns:
  void. The calibration result is delivered through the global at
  0x00069ea8. Stack is balanced by a plain RET (no purge).

Pool: crt  [CLIB3S.LIB(__delay_init) score 25.02, delay.obj, Watcom 10.0/10.0a/10.0b]

Pool hint from block triage: ail

Pool: ail
The 'switch to private stack' half of a Miles AIL hand-written assembly stack-switch pair. Called as (void *stack_base, int stack_size, U16 *old_ss, U32 *old_esp, U32 *old_ebp), it writes the current ESP, EBP and SS through the three out-pointers, computes the new stack top as base+size rounded down, reloads SS from DS so the new stack lives in the flat data selector, moves ESP there, recreates the caller's frame depth (EBP-ESP, plus 0x14 bytes of headroom) on the new stack, discards its own return address and argument block from the old stack with ADD ESP,0x18, and JMPs to the return address so the caller resumes transparently on the private stack. The matching restore half is the immediately following 00044e0f, which takes back exactly the three values (ss, esp, ebp) that this routine saves out.
Evidence: crt is eliminated by direct library evidence rather than by an absent FID hit. A byte search of this function's 18-byte relocation-free head (8b44241089208b44241489288b44240c8c10) and of 00044e0f's head across all 1086 .LIB files under WATCOM_10_series -- including CLIB3S.LIB, MATH387S.LIB and EMU387.LIB of 10.0a, the toolchain fixed by build_flags.md -- returns zero hits, while the control patterns from build_flags.md (the 31-byte uppercase routine at 0x435f3 and __CHP at 0x43657) hit CLIB3S.LIB 16 and 1 times respectively in the same scan. The method therefore finds Watcom library code in this binary and does not find this routine. binary_artifact is out: it is a substantive multi-step primitive with a real calling contract, not a thunk, jump island or compiler helper. fdps is out: the game does contain hand-written assembly, but it is register-argument graphics and audio kernels (the 0x53000-0x57000 RLE blitters and mixers) that are all live, whereas this routine takes five stack arguments in a library-API shape and is completely unreferenced -- get_xrefs_to returns nothing for either half, and a byte search of the image for the little-endian constants d94d0400 and 0f4e0400 finds no pointer to either, so nothing reaches them through a dispatch table or computed jump either. Game-authored assembly that the game never calls is not credible. With three pools eliminated the remaining pool is ail, and the positive picture corroborates it. The routine is byte-contiguous with no padding inside a run of AIL workers: 00044d7b (ail, high) ends at 00044dbf, the AIL lock/unlock pair 00044dc0/00044dc4 (ail, high) runs to 00044dd8, this routine occupies 00044dd9-00044e0e, its partner 00044e0f-00044e2a, and 00044e2b -- called from 0003dd45 inside the function Ghidra has already named AIL_call_driver -- begins immediately after; the next module boundary is 00044f05. Linkers place whole object modules contiguously, so a routine strictly interior to two identified AIL workers with zero padding belongs to the same hand-written AIL assembly object. That also explains the orphan status: the AIL forwarding band emits a per-entry stub only for entries the game actually calls (0003dcb0 is a bare JMP to the 00044dc0 lock worker, 0003dcb5 a push-and-call forwarder to the 00044dc4 unlock worker, and the band then runs straight into other code at 0003dcc3 with no stub for this pair), while the workers themselves all arrive together inside the shared assembly module. Semantically it is the primitive this library demonstrably needs: the AIL USE16 ISR stub at 00044b10 (ail, high) switches DS/ES/SS and ESP to a patched private stack before RETFing into 16-bit driver code, and reloading SS from DS is exactly the flat-model fixup required before handing control to code that assumes SS==DS. Note the packet's __watcall is Ghidra's ANALYSIS guess and carries no weight: the image is built -4s, so stack arguments are the norm for game and library code alike and do not by themselves separate the pools.

=== 0004bced [PLATE]
matching DPMI unlock guard: if (flag_0x61138 != 0) { call dpmi_unlock_linear_region 0x3cb73(0x4b370, 0x4bced); flag = 0; } -- mirror of 0x4b370
Pool hint from block triage: ail

Pool: ail  [Miles AIL/MSS wave-synthesizer (HWAVE) module -- the per-translation-unit VMM UNLOCK marker; no Watcom FID hit because AIL is not in CLIB3S/MATH387S/EMU387]
End-marker half of the Miles AIL per-module DPMI page-lock pair for the wave-synthesizer module: when the module's static 'locked' flag at 0x00061138 is set it calls the AIL unlock-linear-region primitive FUN_0003cb6e(0x4b370, 0x4bced) cdecl-style, releasing the module's own code extent, then clears the flag. Its own address is the extent's end bound.
Evidence: Settled by the neighbours on three independent axes.

(1) The idiom is AIL's, not the game's, and it is established three times over in this binary with both halves judged ail at high confidence: [0x45e10, 0x47740] (DIG driver-installation module), [0x477f4, 0x47e0a] (digital-audio file module, guard 0x610a0), and [0x47e30, 0x4b080] (XMIDI module, guard 0x61128). Miles Sound System places a lock/unlock pair physically first and last in each translation unit so that &self serves as the extent bound, because the module runs at timer-interrupt time and must not page-fault. A read-only disassembly shows this function is that pattern term for term: PUSH EBX / CMP [0x61138],0 / JZ out / PUSH 0x4bced / PUSH 0x4b370 / CALL 0x3cb6e / ADD ESP,8 / MOV [0x61138],0. Its mirror at 0x4b370 is the same instruction sequence inverted (JNZ, CALL 0x3cb01, flag = 1) over the identical extent and the identical guard, so the two are one translation unit by construction. The guard 0x61138 also sits in the same run of per-module lock flags as 0x6109c, 0x610a0 and 0x61128. Having no resolved caller is expected, not anomalous: the parallel end markers 0x47740 and 0x47e0a have none either, since the only references to a module-end marker are the DATA pushes of its address as the extent terminator.

(2) Both callees are ail. FUN_0003cb6e is the DPMI 0x0601 Unlock Linear Region primitive (AIL_vmm_unlock_range shape) and its 0x0600 twin FUN_0003cb01 is ail at high confidence -- both part of the byte-symmetric quartet 0x3cb01/0x3cb6e/0x3cb93/0x3cbaa in the contiguous all-AIL DOS-extender support run at 0x3c9db-0x3ccf7.

(3) Decisively, the bracketed extent is the AIL wave-synthesizer. Of the 2429 bytes between the markers, roughly 80 percent carry ail verdicts, four of them high: FUN_0004bb21 (ail/high) allocates the 0x65c-byte HWAVE descriptor and on malloc failure copies the verbatim Miles error text 'Insufficient memory for HWAVE descriptor' into the AIL_last_error buffer at 0x69ef0, out of the contiguous MSS error-string pool at 0x63452-0x63650; FUN_0004b720 (ail/high) is the module's MIDI channel-event dispatcher, driving the AIL sample API and testing return values against SMP_PLAYING and SMP_DONE; FUN_0004b398 (ail/high) records XMIDI-proprietary sequencer controllers 0x6E, 0x6F, 0x70, 0x72, 0x73 and 0x77, which have no meaning outside Miles; FUN_0004b54d (ail/high) and FUN_0004b6f5 (ail) are the bank+patch timbre-table lookup registered as an AIL callback by FUN_0004bb21 via the callback registrars at 0x41af6/0x41be3. The remaining functions do not pull the other way: FUN_0004bc99 tail-jumps backwards to 0x4bb1a, the shared epilogue of FUN_0004b720, so it is a fragment of that ail/high function, and the two fdps-pooled bodies inside (0x4b580, 0x4b5f0) both name FUN_0004b720 as their only caller and were judged before it was, with 0x4b5f0's own open question explicitly conceding it cannot exclude a third-party sound engine. Under the vendored-.LIB link direction, an AIL object cannot call a game symbol, so an ail/high body inside the extent fixes the extent, and a module's own marker belongs to the module it brackets.

Not crt: fid[] is empty against a database built from the CLIB3S/MATH387S/EMU387 libraries the linker actually used, and Watcom 10.0 ships no DPMI region lock/unlock API -- this is a client of one. Not binary_artifact: it has a static guard, a conditional, a two-argument cdecl call with caller stack cleanup and a global side effect, i.e. genuine C source, not a thunk or jump island. Not fdps: see the extent and link-direction arguments above.

=== 0004c87d [PLATE]

Not fdps: no game data, string or resource reference, and the only path that reaches it is inside printf. === 0004df4c [PLATE]
Watcom C/C++ 10.0a CRT routine __CMain, from library module cmain386 (CLIB3S.LIB).
Byte-identical to the library copy; the externs it references are, in order,
__ASTACKSIZ, stackavail, __ASTACKPTR, __CommonInit, ___Argv, ___Argc, main, exit.

Algorithm:
  1. Load __ASTACKSIZ (0x00060438), round it up to a multiple of 4 ((n + 3) & ~3,
     coded as ADD EBX,3 / AND BL,0FCh).
  2. Call stackavail (0x0004e692, ESP - __STACKLOW at 0x00060430). If the rounded
     size is smaller than the free stack, carve the block off the stack with
     SUB ESP,size and keep the resulting ESP as the block base; otherwise use a
     null base, i.e. no auto-stack is reserved.
  3. Store base + __ASTACKSIZ (the unrounded size) into __ASTACKPTR (0x0006043c).
     In this build __ASTACKSIZ is 0 and __ASTACKPTR is never read back, so the
     whole step is inert here.
  4. Call __CommonInit (0x00054dbc), which sets _amblksiz (0x000613c4) to 0x8000.
  5. Push _argv (0x0006a3b8) then _argc (0x0006a3b4), call main (0x00029220),
     clean the two arguments off the stack, then push main's return value and
     call exit (0x00042e0f).

Control never comes back: exit runs the atexit/fini chains and terminates. The
epilogue (MOV ESP,EBP / POP EBP / POP EBX / RET) exists only to restore the frame
and the saved EBX and is unreachable in practice.

The single caller is the DOS/4G CRT startup at 0x00043310, which invokes
__InitRtns(255) at 0x0004dfa6, then this function, then __FiniRtns(0,255) at
0x0004dff1 before the INT 21h/AH=4Ch fallback.

Parameters: none. EBX and EBP are callee-saved here, not inputs; every other
register is written before it is read, and RET performs no stack purge.

Returns: nothing (void). The function does not return to its caller.

Pool: crt  [CLIB3S.LIB(__CMain) score 33.68, cmain386.obj, Watcom 10.0/10.0a/10.0b]
Watcom C startup glue: reserves the requested stack margin, runs the runtime initialiser list, calls main(argc, argv) with the saved argument globals, and passes its return value to exit().
Evidence: The body is the textbook Watcom __CMain sequence: read the stack-size global at 0x00060438, round up to a dword, compare against stackavail (crt_stackavail@0004e692) and carve the margin off ESP, store the resulting stack base at 0x0006043c, call the runtime initialiser chain (crt_common_init@00054dbc), then push the argv/argc globals (0x0006a3b8/0x0006a3b4) and call main@00029220, finally push the return value into crt_exit@00042e0f. Its only caller is crt_cstart_body@00043310, the C startup entry. Everything it touches is runtime state, not game state; the fact that it calls main is the documented startup exception, not evidence of game code. Not binary_artifact: 89 bytes of real logic with a genuine library symbol. Nothing AIL-related is referenced.

=== 0004dfa6 [PLATE]
Watcom C runtime __InitRtns -- run the link-time initialiser table.

Algorithm:
The linker gathers records of the form

    struct rt_init { unsigned char rtn_type;      /* 2 == already run */
                     unsigned char priority;
                     void (*rtn)( void ); };      /* 6 bytes each */

into a contiguous "XI" table. Here that table spans 0x000638f0
(inclusive) to 0x00063920 (exclusive), i.e. 8 entries; a matching
"YI" rundown table begins at 0x00063920 and is walked by the
termination routine at 0x0004dff1.

Outer loop, repeated until no candidate remains:
  - set the running minimum priority to the caller-supplied bound and
    the selected entry to the table end (the "nothing found" sentinel);
  - scan the whole table forward; an entry is a candidate when its
    rtn_type is not 2 (not yet executed) and its priority is <= the
    running minimum, in which case it becomes the new selection and
    lowers the minimum. Because the test is <= rather than <, a later
    entry with a priority equal to the current minimum displaces an
    earlier one, so entries sharing a priority execute in reverse
    table order;
  - if nothing was selected, return;
  - otherwise reload ES from DS, call the entry's function pointer
    when it is non-NULL, and stamp rtn_type = 2 so the entry is never
    run twice.

The current table holds eight entries, all rtn_type 0, with priorities
0x01 (0x0003d50a), 0x02 (0x00044749) and six at 0x20 (0x00043c82,
0x0004cfc8, 0x0004e040, 0x00043612, 0x00054893, 0x00054f86).

Parameters:
  EAX (only AL is used) -- the priority ceiling. Entries whose
  priority exceeds it are skipped. The startup code at 0x00043310
  passes 0xff, i.e. "run everything".

Returns:
  Nothing. ESI, EDI, EBX, EDX and the ES segment register are saved on
  entry and restored before returning.

Pool: crt  [CLIB3S.LIB(__InitRtns) score 41.02, inirt386.obj, Watcom 10.0/10.0a/10.0b]
Walks the Watcom startup initialiser table between 0x638f0 and 0x63920, repeatedly selecting the lowest-priority entry not yet marked done whose priority is within the requested limit, calling its function pointer with DS reloaded into ES, and marking the record as executed.
Evidence: The disassembly is the textbook Watcom __InitRtns loop: a table of 6-byte records (status byte, priority byte, 4-byte routine pointer), scanning ESI from the table start 0x638f0 to the end 0x63920, skipping records whose status byte is already 2, tracking the record with the smallest priority byte <= the priority argument passed in AL (__watcall), then PUSH DS/POP ES, CALL EAX through the record's pointer, store 2 into the status byte and restart the scan until nothing is left. That is pure C runtime startup machinery, not game logic: the only caller is crt_cstart_body@00043310 (the CRT startup body) and the only callee is crt_init_delay@00043c82, both already crt. The Function ID hit __InitRtns (score 41.02, inirt386.obj) matches this behaviour exactly. It is far too large and structured to be a linker thunk or compiler helper, and it touches no AIL driver state or DOS interrupt path.

=== 0004e692 [PLATE]
Watcom C runtime: stackavail() -- report remaining stack space.

Algorithm:
  Copies ESP into EAX and subtracts the global stack-low limit stored at
  0x00060430, then returns. Because ESP at function entry already points at
  this call's own return address, the reported figure is 4 bytes smaller than
  the space the caller actually has, which is conservative and harmless.
  The same 0x00060430 global is the limit used by the compiler-generated
  stack-overflow probe at 0x0004362d (which tests ESP-size against it) and is
  initialised by the startup code at 0x000434c0, confirming it is __STACKLOW
  rather than a stack base or margin constant.

  All three callers are CRT internals that use the result to choose between an
  on-stack scratch buffer and the heap: 0x0004df4c and 0x000556a9 both compare
  (size + 3) & ~3 against the return value before pointing their buffer at a
  local array or at NULL, and 0x00043ab4 (the DOS int 21h AH=40h write path
  with LF->CRLF translation) calls the stack-overflow handler at 0x0004364b
  when fewer than 0xB0 bytes remain and otherwise picks a 0x200-byte staging
  buffer when at least 0x230 bytes are free, falling back to 0x80 bytes.

Parameters:
  None. EAX is written before any register is read, and no argument register
  or stack slot is consumed.

Returns:
  EAX = bytes of stack remaining below the current stack pointer, as an
  unsigned value. Every caller treats it as unsigned.

Pool: crt  [CLIB3S.LIB(stackavail), no FID hit (9-byte function below matcher threshold); identified by exact instruction-for-instruction match with Watcom stackav.asm]
Returns the number of bytes of stack still available by subtracting the stack-low limit global at 0x00060430 from the current ESP.
Evidence: The whole body is MOV EAX,ESP / SUB EAX,[0x00060430] / RET, which is byte-for-byte the Watcom C library stackavail() implementation (esp - __STACKLOW) and returns in EAX per __watcall. The referenced global 0x00060430 is the runtime's __STACKLOW, a CRT-owned variable, not game data; there is no game state, no DOS interrupt path, no .DIG driver structure and no 0x70000 access, ruling out fdps and ail. It is not a binary_artifact because it is not a thunk or jump island: it computes and returns a value and corresponds to a real library source function with a real Watcom symbol. One of its callers is already identified as crt_cmain@0004df4c, consistent with runtime-internal use.
Open question: The two other callers (FUN_000556a9, FUN_00043ab4) are still unnamed, so it is unconfirmed whether stackavail is also reached from game code; this does not change the pool of this function.

Open question: The exact upstream Miles AIL symbol for this particular mixer variant is unknown, so no name is proposed; identifying the whole 0x52a40 table's variants together (index 8 of 16) would give the real names.

=== 000538df [PLATE]
Pool: ail  [Miles AIL/MSS -- DIG (digital audio) module, sample mix-in bank of the software mixer, dispatched from the bank base at 0x00052a5c; no Function ID hit because AIL ships in its own library, not CLIB3S/MATH387S/EMU387]
Slot 2 of the Miles AIL DIG mixer's sample mix-in bank based at 0x00052a5c: the unscaled, non-resampling accumulate stage for an 8-bit stereo source feeding a mono mix accumulator. Per frame it loads the left sample into AH and the right sample into BH, converts both from offset-binary to signed 16-bit with XOR 0x8000, advances ESI by 2 (one 8-bit stereo frame), sign-extends the left sample into EBP and adds it into the single 32-bit accumulator at [EDI], advancing EDI by 4 (one mono accumulator slot per frame). It runs until the source cursor reaches the source-end pointer at 0x00061500 or the destination cursor reaches the mix-buffer-end pointer at 0x00061508, both of which its dispatcher writes immediately before the call. The right channel is loaded and converted but not summed, because this slot's output is mono: the stereo-source loader is the form shared across the bank, and the mono-output slots drop the second channel rather than downmix it.
Evidence: The consumer chain is now resolved read-only and it is AIL. get_xrefs_to on 000538df returns exactly one DATA reference, from 0x00052a64, plus this function's own loop-back JC at 0x00053908. 0x00052a64 is not a table base: it is slot (0x52a64 - 0x52a5c) / 4 = 2 of the mix-in bank based at 0x00052a5c, and the one instruction in the whole program that indexes that base is CALL dword ptr [EBP*0x4 + 0x52a5c] at 0x000546a0 inside FUN_00054564 -- a search_instructions sweep for indexed CALLs returns only four program-wide, of which this is the one covering this address. FUN_00054564 already carries an independent ail/high verdict as the AIL routine that serves one digital sample: it derives the mixer-selection flag word from the sample and driver formats, volume and pan, computes the 16.16 rate delta, and calls the indexed mixer routine. Its sole caller is FUN_000461d0, itself ail/high as the interrupt-time DIG mixer service that walks the driver's sample array at stride 0x894 and flips the double buffer. FUN_00054564 also writes the exact two globals this body reads: 0x00061508 at 0x0005464c as driver mix buffer [+0x50] plus its size [+0x4c], and 0x00061500 at 0x0005466f as the current source block base plus its length. It stores the selection word into 0x000614f8, the same global the sibling output-converter dispatcher uses, so the mix-in bank and the output-converter bank at 0x0005285c are one subsystem. FUN_00054823 DPMI-page-locks precisely both halves of it -- the data range 0x614f8..0x61518, which contains 0x61500 and 0x61508, and the code range 0x5285c..0x54823, which contains this body -- through FUN_0003cb01, which is ail/high as the AIL_vmm_lock_range primitive, and is reached from FUN_00045e10, ail/high as the DIG driver-installation module's own lock routine that chains to it. Resident-at-interrupt-time page locking of a mixer bank plus its state is Miles AIL module structure.

The slot number then decodes this body bit for bit, which makes the identification specific rather than circumstantial. FUN_00054564 builds the index at 0x000545cc from: bit 0x1 when driver format [+0x18] is 2 or 3, i.e. stereo output; bit 0x2 when sample format [+0x34] is 2 or 3, i.e. stereo source; bit 0x8 when [+0x34] is 1 or 3, i.e. 16-bit source; bit 0x10 / bit 0x40 from the volume 0x7f and pan 0x40 default test at 0x000545af; bit 0x20 set at 0x0005463a only when the 16.16 rate delta differs enough from unity to need resampling. Slot 2 is bit 0x2 alone. Bit 0x2 set, stereo source -- and the body reads two bytes per frame, [ESI] and [ESI+1], stepping ESI by 2. Bit 0x1 clear, mono output -- and it touches a single accumulator at [EDI] stepping by 4, not a left/right pair at stride 8 like the stereo-output siblings. Bit 0x8 clear, 8-bit source -- and it loads bytes into the high half and applies XOR 0x8000, the offset-binary to signed conversion for 8-bit PCM. Bit 0x20 clear, no resampling -- and the source cursor walks straight without touching the 16.16 state at 0x0006150c/0x00061510/0x00061514 that the dispatcher prepares for the resampling slots. Bits 0x10 and 0x40 clear, default volume and centre pan -- and the accumulation is a plain ADD with no multiply or scaling table. Every bit of the index matches, and nothing in the body is left unexplained.

The other three pools stay excluded. fid[] is empty and no CLIB3S/MATH387S/EMU387 routine accumulates PCM samples into a mix buffer, so not crt. It is a real 44-byte loop doing offset-binary conversion, sign extension and accumulation, with its own RET, not a thunk, jump island or compiler helper, so not binary_artifact. Not fdps: it has no prologue and no stack frame, takes its operands preset in ESI/EDI and its bounds in two driver-written globals, and clobbers callee-saved EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP, which wcc386 cannot emit under __watcall despite the ANALYSIS-guessed convention in the packet; its only consumer is AIL DIG driver code, and no game-side function reaches the bank. The emit ticket must carry it as assembly rather than reconstruct it as C.

=== 00054dbc [PLATE]
Watcom CRT __CommonInit, identified by position in __CMain's extern order
(__ASTACKSIZ, stackavail, __ASTACKPTR, __CommonInit, ___Argv, ___Argc, main,
exit) rather than by its body, which shows only the _amblksiz store below.

Watcom C runtime helper: install the default heap growth granularity.

Algorithm:
  Stores the constant 0x8000 (32768) into the global at 0x000613c4 and returns.
  That global is the Watcom CRT variable `_amblksiz`, the minimum amount by
  which the heap manager grows the heap when it has to ask the system for more
  memory. Identification of the global rests on two other users of it:
    - 0x0004442b (heap grow helper) clamps a requested growth amount up to
      `_amblksiz` (with the low bit masked off, the documented Watcom flag bit)
      and then rounds the result up to a 4 KiB page boundary.
    - 0x0005600f (Watcom __cenvarg, the DOS spawn/exec command line and
      environment block builder) saves the global, forces it to 16 while it
      allocates the tightly sized argument block, and restores it afterwards -
      the exact save/set-16/restore idiom of the library source.
  The image initialises the global to 16; this routine raises it to 32 KiB so
  that a DOS extender heap is grown in large chunks instead of many small
  extender calls. It is called from the CRT startup path (0x0004df4c, which
  sizes the stack, then calls main at 0x00029220 and passes its result to exit
  at 0x00042e0f), so it runs exactly once before user code starts.

Parameters:
  None. The function reads no register and no stack slot.

Returns:
  Nothing. Only the global at 0x000613c4 is modified; no register is written.

Pool: crt
Stores the constant 0x8000 into the runtime global at 0x000613c4 and returns, an initialisation step run from the Watcom C startup path.
Evidence: The whole body is MOV dword ptr [0x000613c4],0x8000 / RET (matches head_hex c705c413060000800000c3). It is not a thunk or jump island and it writes a runtime global rather than dispatching, so binary_artifact does not fit; there is no DOS interrupt path, .DIG driver structure or 0x70000 state access, so ail is excluded. Open question: No Function ID hit, so the exact Watcom symbol is unidentified; DAT_000613c4 is still unnamed (the 0x8000 constant looks like a heap/stack granularity or amblksiz-style tuning value), so no library symbol name is proposed.

=== 000567f0 [PLATE]
Installs the game's keyboard (INT 09h / IRQ1) interrupt handler.

Algorithm:
  1. Saves DS and ES.
  2. INT 21h with EAX=0x3509 (DOS Get Interrupt Vector, vector 09h). Under
     DOS/4G this returns the protected-mode vector in ES:EBX.
  3. Stores the returned handler offset (EBX) at 0x00070002 and the returned
     selector (ES) at 0x00070000, so the old vector can be restored later.
  4. Loads DS from CS so DS:EDX addresses code in this module, points EDX at
     the handler 0x00056837, and issues INT 21h with AH=0x25, AL=0x09 (DOS Set
     Interrupt Vector) to hook IRQ1.
  5. Restores ES and DS and returns.

Hand-written assembly: it manipulates segment registers directly and passes
arguments to DOS in explicit registers, which the C compiler would not emit.

Parameters: none.
Returns: nothing.

Pool: fdps
Saves the old INT 9 (keyboard) vector via DOS INT 21h AH=35h into the dword/word pair at 0x00070002/0x00070000, then installs the game's own INT 9 handler at CS:0x00056837 with INT 21h AH=25h.
Evidence: Hand-written inline-asm-style real-mode DOS vector hook: PUSH DS/ES, MOV EAX,0x3509, INT 21h, store old vector, PUSH CS/POP DS, MOV EDX,0x56837, AH=25h, INT 21h, restore. No fid hits at all against CLIB3S/MATH387S/EMU387. The Watcom CRT never hooks INT 9, and Miles AIL hooks the timer/driver path rather than the keyboard, so neither crt nor ail fits. It is 40 bytes of real work with a stored handler address, not a thunk or jump island, so not binary_artifact. All three callers are game code (fdps_load_global_resources, fdps_play_movie, fdps_cd_verify_disc_and_play_track), which is exactly the pattern of a game-owned input hook re-armed around movie/CD playback. The 0x00070000 area used here holds the saved INT 9 vector, unrelated to any AIL state usage of that region.

=== 00056837 [PLATE]
Keyboard IRQ1 interrupt service routine (protected mode, DOS/4G).

Installed by fdps_install_keyboard_isr at 0005680a; it is never called
directly, only entered through the interrupt vector, and exits with IRETD.

Algorithm:
  1. STI, then save EDX/ECX/EBX/EAX and DS on the interrupt stack, and load
     DS with selector 0x0002 so the handler can reach the program data
     segment regardless of the interrupted context.
  2. IN AL,0x60 reads the raw scancode; it is stored unconditionally in the
     last-scancode byte at 0x00070006.
  3. IN AL,0x61, set bit 7, OUT it back, then clear bit 7 and OUT again --
     the classic XT-style keyboard acknowledge strobe on port 0x61.
  4. Compare the new scancode with the previous one at 0x00070021. If they
     are equal, nothing is queued (this suppresses the auto-repeat stream and
     duplicate reports). Otherwise the new value becomes the previous one.
  5. If the scancode is below 0x80 (a make code, i.e. key press rather than
     the 0x80-or-above break code), store it into the byte ring buffer that
     begins at 0x0007000f, indexed by the write cursor at 0x0007001d, then
     increment the cursor and wrap it to 0 when it reaches 10. The buffer has
     10 entries and the cursor is a pure write index -- the consumer side
     tracks its own read position.
  6. OUT 0x20,0x20 sends the non-specific EOI to the master PIC.
  7. Restore DS and the four saved registers and return with IRETD.

Note that break codes and repeats only update the last-scancode bytes; they
never enter the ring buffer. The original interrupt handler is not chained.

Parameters:
  None. Entered from the interrupt gate, not by a call, so no arguments are
  passed in registers or on the stack. The decompiler's invented param_1 is
  the interrupt frame and is not real.

Returns:
  Nothing. Exits with IRETD; all side effects are in the globals at
  0x00070006 (last scancode), 0x00070021 (previous scancode for the repeat
  filter), 0x0007000f (10-byte scancode ring buffer) and 0x0007001d (ring
  write index).

Pool: fdps
Custom INT 9 keyboard interrupt handler: reads the scancode from port 0x60, pulses the keyboard acknowledge bit on port 0x61, stores the raw scancode, and on a make code different from the previous one appends it to a 10-entry circular key buffer before issuing the PIC EOI to port 0x20 and returning with IRETD.
Evidence: Disassembly is an unambiguous hardware ISR: STI, saves EDX/ECX/EBX/EAX and DS, reloads DS with the flat data selector 0x2, IN AL,0x60 / IN AL,0x61 keyboard-controller sequence, EOI (MOV AL,0x20; OUT 0x20,AL) and IRETD. It maintains game-owned state at 0x70006 (last raw scancode), 0x70021 (previous key, debounce), 0x7000f (10-byte circular scancode buffer) and 0x7001d (write index, wrapped at 0xa). No fid hits at all, and the Watcom CRT (CLIB3S/MATH387S/EMU387) contains no INT 9 keyboard handler; Miles AIL hooks the timer and the sound driver, never the keyboard, and this touches no .DIG driver structure. An IRETD entry point with a hand-rolled key ring buffer is exactly the game's own input layer, not a linker thunk or compiler helper, so binary_artifact is excluded too. Consistent with the existing subsys_input / backbone tagging.

=== 000568b7 [PLATE]
Algorithm: Runs a self-inverse XOR stream cipher over a byte buffer in place. A 16-bit key register is seeded with 0xA5. For each of len bytes: key = rol16(key + 0x9014, 3), then the source byte is XORed with the low 8 bits of key and stored back at the same offset (the assembly uses LODSB/STOSB with ESI and EDI both initialised from buf, so it is strictly in place). The key stream depends only on the byte index, never on the data, so the same call both encrypts and decrypts. The loop is driven by LOOP with the count in ECX, so a length of 0 wraps and processes 0x100000000 bytes; callers must pass a positive length. Written as hand-tuned assembly with stack-passed arguments rather than the Watcom register convention used elsewhere in the module.

Parameters: buf - pointer to the buffer to transform in place; len - number of bytes to process, must be greater than zero.

Returns: nothing; the buffer is modified in place.

Pool: fdps
In-place XOR stream cipher over a buffer: seeds DX with 0xa5, then per byte adds 0x9014 to DX, rotates DX left by 3, and XORs the byte with DL using LODSB/STOSB/LOOP.
Evidence: No Function ID hit at all against CLIB3S/MATH387S/EMU387/GRAPH. The body is a game-specific keystream with hardcoded magic constants (0xa5 seed, 0x9014 addend, ROL 3) that matches no C runtime or Miles AIL routine; nothing in CLIB3S does obfuscation, and it touches no DOS interrupt path, no .DIG driver structure and no 0x70000 AIL state. === 000568db [PLATE]
Blit mode dispatcher: publishes the blit geometry into the shared graphics globals and jumps into the inner copy loop chosen by the mode byte.

Algorithm:
  Loads the source pointer into ESI and the destination pointer into EDI, which the mode handlers consume directly as x86 string-operation registers. Stores the destination pitch (arg 5) into the word at 0x0007002e, the run width (arg 3) into the word at 0x00070024, and the row count (arg 4) into the word at 0x00070022, then computes EDX = pitch - width, the number of bytes to advance the destination pointer at the end of each row. Clears EAX and ECX and loads the mode byte (arg 7) into BH. A linear chain of compares on BH selects one of thirteen handlers for modes 0 through 12 (0x00056a0d, 0x00056a8d, 0x00056b25, 0x00056bb7, 0x00056c5e, 0x00056e2a, 0x00057114, 0x00057551, 0x000575ed, 0x0005761b, 0x00057793, 0x00057916, 0x00057a74); every branch converges on the common epilogue, and a mode byte above 12 falls through and draws nothing. The handlers are called, not tail-jumped, so the frame pointer set up here stays live for them; the sixth argument at [EBP+0x1c] is never touched by this function and is presumably read from that frame by individual handlers.

Parameters:
  src    - source pixel data, loaded into ESI
  dst    - destination surface pointer, loaded into EDI
  width  - bytes copied per row, also stored to the global at 0x00070024
  height - number of rows, also stored to the global at 0x00070022
  pitch  - destination stride, stored to the global at 0x0007002e; pitch - width is passed to the handler in EDX
  arg6   - unused by this function, left on the frame for the handlers
  mode   - blit mode selector, 0 through 12; other values are a no-op

Returns:
  Nothing. All output goes to the destination surface and the shared blit globals.

Pool: fdps
